title: Measurement of charged-particle production in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}=9.62$ TeV proton-oxygen collisions as a probe of cosmic-ray air showers with the ATLAS detector
comment: 36 pages in total, author list starting page 19, 2 figures, submitted to Phys. Rev. Lett. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/STDM-2025-08
summary: This Letter presents a measurement of prompt charged-particle production in proton-oxygen interactions at $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}=9.62$ TeV center-of-mass energy with the ATLAS detector, corresponding to 634 $μ$b$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity. A total of 246 million selected events have at least one track with transverse momentum $p_\text{T}> 500$ MeV and pseudorapidity $|η|<2.5$. The measured fiducial proton-oxygen cross section is $σ_\text{fid.}^{p\text{O}}=396 \pm 6~(\text{exp.}) \pm 9~(\text{lumi.})~\text{mb}$ and the extrapolated inelastic proton-air cross section is $σ^{p+\text{air}}_\text{inel.} = 406 \pm 6~(\text{exp.}) \pm 9~(\text{lumi.}) \pm 28~(\text{th.})~\text{mb}$. Measurements of charged-particle multiplicity, $p_\text{T}$, and $η$ distributions are an order-of-magnitude more precise than differences between hadronic-interaction models. These results enable improved modeling of cosmic-ray air showers, which is important for astroparticle physics.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a high-precision measurement of prompt charged-particle production in proton-oxygen collisions at √s_NN = 9.62 TeV using ATLAS, yielding improved constraints on hadronic interaction models and cosmic-ray air shower simulations.
AI.motivation: To provide precise experimental data on proton-nucleus interactions to test and improve hadronic-interaction models used in cosmic-ray air shower simulations—critical for astroparticle physics.
AI.method: Measurement of charged-particle production (multiplicity, p_T, η distributions) in proton-oxygen collisions at √s_NN = 9.62 TeV with ATLAS; selection of 246 million events with p_T > 500 MeV and |η| < 2.5; fiducial cross section extraction and extrapolation to inelastic proton-air cross section using Glauber modeling.
AI.result: Fiducial pO cross section: σ_fid^pO = 396 ± 6 (exp.) ± 9 (lumi.) mb; extrapolated inelastic p+air cross section: σ_inel^p+air = 406 ± 6 (exp.) ± 9 (lumi.) ± 28 (th.) mb; multiplicity, p_T, and η distributions are an order-of-magnitude more precise than model differences.
AI.conclusion: The results significantly constrain hadronic-interaction models and enhance the reliability of cosmic-ray air shower simulations, advancing astroparticle physics.

title: Measurement of the CKM angle $γ$ in $B^{\pm} \rightarrow D(\rightarrow K^{0}_{\rm S} h^{\prime+}h^{\prime-})h^{\pm}$ decays with a novel approach
comment: All figures and tables, along with machine-readable versions and any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lbfence.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/3989/ (LHCb public pages)
summary: A measurement of the CKM angle $γ$ and related strong-phase parameters is performed using a novel, model-independent approach in ${B^{\pm}\rightarrow D(\rightarrow K^{0}_{\rm S} h^{\prime+}h^{\prime-}) h^{\pm}}$ decays, where $h^{(\prime)} \equiv π, K$. The analysis uses a joint data sample of electron-positron collisions collected by the BESIII experiment at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider II during 2010--2011 and 2021--2022, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 8 fb$^{-1}$, and proton-proton collisions collected by the LHCb experiment at the Large Hadron Collider during 2011--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9 fb$^{-1}$. The two datasets are analyzed simultaneously by applying per-event weights based on the amplitude variation over the $D$-decay phase space to enhance the sensitivity to $C\!P$-violating observables. The CKM angle $γ$ is determined to be $γ= (71.3\pm 5.0)^{\circ}$, which constitutes the most precise single measurement to date.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the most precise single measurement of the CKM angle γ = (71.3 ± 5.0)° using a model-independent analysis of B± → D(→ K⁰ₛ h′⁺h′⁻) h± decays, combining BESIII (e⁺e⁻, 8 fb⁻¹) and LHCb (pp, 9 fb⁻¹) datasets with per-event amplitude-weighted joint fitting to enhance CP-violation sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To achieve a high-precision, model-independent determination of the CKM angle γ — a fundamental parameter in the Standard Model governing CP violation in quark mixing — free from theoretical uncertainties associated with hadronic strong-phase modeling.
AI.method: A model-independent amplitude analysis of B± → D(→ K⁰ₛ h′⁺h′⁻) h± (h′, h = π, K) decays; simultaneous fit to BESIII (2010–2011, 2021–2022; 8 fb⁻¹) and LHCb (2011–2018; 9 fb⁻¹) datasets using per-event weights derived from the variation of the D-decay amplitude over its phase space to maximize sensitivity to CP-violating observables.
AI.result: γ = (71.3 ± 5.0)°, the most precise single measurement of γ to date; improved constraints on related strong-phase parameters via the same model-independent framework.
AI.conclusion: The joint, amplitude-weighted analysis of complementary e⁺e⁻ and pp datasets enables a significant gain in precision for γ without relying on theoretical D-decay models, validating a robust, data-driven approach for future CKM studies.

title: Precise measurement of the CKM angle $γ$ with a novel approach
comment: All figures and tables, along with machine-readable versions and any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lbfence.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/5991/ (LHCb public pages)
summary: A measurement of the CKM angle $γ$ is performed by applying a novel, unbinned, model-independent approach to datasets of electron-positron collisions collected by the BESIII experiment and proton-proton collisions by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 8 fb$^{-1}$ and 9 fb$^{-1}$, respectively. The $C\!P$-violating phase $γ$ is determined from ${B^{\pm}\rightarrow D(\rightarrow K_{\rm S}^{0} h^{\prime+}h^{\prime-}) h^{\pm}}$ decays in LHCb data, where $h^{(\prime)}$ is either a pion or kaon, while the corresponding strong-phase parameters are measured using doubly tagged ${D\rightarrow K_{\rm S/L}^0 h^{\prime+} h^{\prime-}}$ decays in the quantum-correlated $D\overline{D}$ system present in BESIII data. A joint fit to both datasets, which allows for a simultaneous determination of the associated $C\!P$-violating observables and strong-phase parameters, yields ${γ= (71.3\pm 5.0)^{\circ}}$. The result is the most precise to date and consistent with previous measurements and world averages.

AI.tldr: A novel, unbinned, model-independent method is used to measure the CKM angle γ using BESIII (e⁺e⁻) and LHCb (pp) data; strong-phase parameters are constrained from quantum-correlated D̅D decays at BESIII, while CP violation is extracted from B± → D(→ KS⁰h′+h′−)h± at LHCb; joint fit yields γ = 71.3 ± 5.0°, the most precise single measurement to date.
AI.motivation: To improve precision and reduce model dependence in the determination of the CKM angle γ, a key parameter for testing the Standard Model and probing new physics via CP violation in B decays.
AI.method: Unbinned, model-independent analysis combining LHCb data (9 fb⁻¹ pp collisions) for B± → D(→ KS⁰h′+h′−)h± decays and BESIII data (8 fb⁻¹ e⁺e⁻ collisions) for doubly tagged D → KS/L⁰h′+h′− decays in quantum-correlated D̅D events; simultaneous joint fit constrains both γ and D-decay strong-phase parameters.
AI.result: γ = (71.3 ± 5.0)°, with uncertainty dominated by statistical and systematic contributions from both experiments; highest precision single measurement of γ to date.
AI.conclusion: The result confirms Standard Model consistency, sets a new benchmark for γ precision, and validates the model-independent, multi-experiment fitting strategy for future CP-violation studies.

title: Reactor Antineutrino Oscillations and Geoneutrinos in SNO+
comment: This contribution was presented as a talk at NuPhys2026
summary: SNO+ is a multipurpose liquid-scintillator neutrino detector located 2 km underground at SNOLAB, Canada. Three large nuclear reactors at baselines of 240-350 km allow a precise measurement of the neutrino oscillation parameter $Δm^2_{21}$ and, to a lesser extent, $θ_{12}$. A spectral analysis is performed, simultaneously fitting $Δm^2_{21}$, $θ_{12}$, the reactor antineutrino flux, background rates, and associated systematics. Using data collected between May 2022 and July 2025, corresponding to a livetime of 685 days, a value of $Δm^2_{21} = (7.93^{+0.21}_{-0.24}) \times 10^{-5}$ eV$^2$ is obtained. This result is compatible with other long-baseline reactor antineutrino measurements by KamLAND and JUNO. SNO+ has also made the first measurement of the geoneutrino flux in the Western Hemisphere, measuring $49^{+13}_{-12}$ TNU, in agreement with predictions from geological models.

AI.tldr: SNO+ measures neutrino oscillation parameters Δm²₂₁ and θ₁₂ via reactor antineutrinos at 240–350 km baselines, yielding Δm²₂₁ = (7.93⁺⁰·²¹₋₀·₂₄)×10⁻⁵ eV²; it also reports the first Western Hemisphere geoneutrino flux: 49⁺¹³₋₁₂ TNU.
AI.motivation: To precisely determine the solar neutrino oscillation parameters Δm²₂₁ and θ₁₂ using reactor antineutrinos, and to measure geoneutrinos—probes of Earth's radiogenic heat—especially in the under-sampled Western Hemisphere.
AI.method: Spectral analysis of reactor antineutrino events detected in the SNO+ liquid-scintillator detector (2 km underground at SNOLAB), simultaneously fitting Δm²₂₁, θ₁₂, reactor flux, backgrounds, and systematic uncertainties using 685 days of livetime data (May 2022–July 2025).
AI.result: Δm²₂₁ = (7.93⁺⁰·²¹₋₀·₂₄)×10⁻⁵ eV²; geoneutrino flux = 49⁺¹³₋₁₂ TNU (first in Western Hemisphere). Both results are consistent with KamLAND/JUNO and geological predictions.
AI.conclusion: SNO+ provides a competitive, independent measurement of Δm²₂₁, confirming the global oscillation picture, and establishes geoneutrino detection capability in the Americas—enabling future studies of Earth's mantle composition and radiogenic power.

title: Spectrum-Generating Algebra in Higher Dimensional Gauge Theories
comment: Proceedings of the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025)
summary: Non-equilibrium properties of strongly interacting gauge theories are often intractable with classical simulation methods. Due to recent developments of quantum simulations, studies of their properties in two spatial dimensions are becoming accessible. By demonstrating the existence of an approximate spectrum-generating algebra for a pure gauge plaquette ladder, we predict and verify the existence of Quantum Many-Body Scars in spin-1 Quantum Link Models. The analysis of the model is facilitated by a dualization process that maps the original gauge theory to a constrained spin chain. Was it not for the constraint, the system would have an exact spectrum-generating algebra. We propose a set of observables for diagnosing an approximate spectrum-generating algebra, which is expected to guide quantum simulators toward interesting physical regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies Quantum Many-Body Scars in spin-1 Quantum Link Models via an approximate spectrum-generating algebra, enabled by dualization to a constrained spin chain and supported by quantum simulation prospects.
AI.motivation: Strongly interacting gauge theories out of equilibrium are classically intractable; quantum simulations now enable access to their 2D non-equilibrium dynamics, motivating the search for analytically tractable structures like spectrum-generating algebras and scars.
AI.method: The authors dualize a pure gauge plaquette ladder to a constrained spin chain, identify an approximate spectrum-generating algebra (broken by the Gauss-law constraint), use it to predict Quantum Many-Body Scars, and propose observables to diagnose the algebra's approximation quality.
AI.result: Existence of Quantum Many-Body Scars is both predicted and verified in spin-1 Quantum Link Models; an approximate spectrum-generating algebra is established; diagnostic observables for the algebra’s validity are proposed.
AI.conclusion: Approximate symmetries—here encoded in an approximate spectrum-generating algebra—can underpin non-ergodic behavior (scars) even in constrained gauge models, offering a pathway to control and probe non-equilibrium quantum dynamics on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Near-Tsirelson Bell-CHSH Violations in Quantum Field Theory via Carleman and Hankel Operators
summary: We study Bell-Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (Bell-CHSH) violations in the vacuum state of free spinor fields in $(1+1)$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. We construct explicit smooth compactly supported test functions with spacelike separated supports whose Bell-CHSH correlators converge to Tsirelson's bound $2\sqrt2$. In the massless case, after passage to the time-zero slice and a natural symmetry reduction, the problem reduces to the quadratic form of the Carleman operator on $L^2([0,\infty))$. Near-maximal Bell violation is then governed by the spectral edge $π$, and explicit near-extremizers are obtained from compactly supported cutoffs of the generalized eigenfunction $x^{-1/2}$. This also explains the appearance of the constant $π$ in earlier wavelet-based formulations. In the massive case, the same reduction leads to a Hankel operator with kernel $mK_1(m(x+y))$, where $K_1$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind of order $1$, and exponentially damped variants of the massless test functions again yield Bell-CHSH values converging to $2\sqrt2$. Therefore, we establish a direct link between Bell-CHSH violations for free $(1+1)$-dimensional spinor fields and the spectral theory of Carleman and Hankel operators on the half-line.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the vacuum state of free spinor fields in (1+1)D Minkowski spacetime exhibits near-maximal Bell-CHSH violations (approaching Tsirelson's bound 2√2) using compactly supported, spacelike-separated test functions; it establishes a rigorous connection to spectral properties of Carleman (massless) and Hankel (massive) operators on L²([0,∞)).
AI.motivation: To rigorously quantify Bell-CHSH violation in relativistic quantum field theory vacua—specifically for free spinor fields—and to uncover the underlying operator-theoretic structure governing maximal violation.
AI.method: Constructs explicit smooth, compactly supported, spacelike-separated test functions; performs time-zero reduction and symmetry analysis; reduces the Bell-CHSH correlator to quadratic forms of the Carleman operator (massless case) and a Hankel operator with kernel mK₁(m(x+y)) (massive case); analyzes spectral edge behavior and uses generalized eigenfunctions (e.g., x⁻¹⁄²) and exponentially damped variants to achieve near-extremal values.
AI.result: Bell-CHSH correlators converge to Tsirelson’s bound 2√2 in both massless and massive cases; the massless case is governed by the spectral edge π of the Carleman operator, explaining prior appearances of π in wavelet approaches; the massive case maps to a Hankel operator whose spectrum supports analogous near-maximal violation.
AI.conclusion: Bell-CHSH violation in the vacuum of (1+1)D free spinor fields is fundamentally tied to the spectral theory of Carleman and Hankel integral operators on the half-line, providing a precise mathematical framework for relativistic entanglement in QFT.

title: Global Dynamical Structure of Einstein$-$Scalar Cosmological Systems
summary: In this work, a global dynamical analysis of spatially flat FLRW cosmologies driven by a canonical scalar field minimally coupled to gravity is presented. Under suitable regularity and asymptotic assumptions on the scalar field potential, it is shown that the Einstein$-$scalar evolution admits no forward trajectory along which the potential steepness becomes asymptotically unbounded. This establishes forward boundedness of the scalar sector and yields the existence of a compact absorbing set for the induced cosmological flow. Using techniques from invariant manifold theory and dissipative dynamical systems, the evolution is shown to admit a compact global attractor governing the late time dynamics of all physically admissible solutions. The asymptotic behavior is further characterized by convergence toward a scalar field dominated invariant manifold, leading to a reduction in effective dynamical dimensionality. In particular, the late time dynamics is governed by at most two independent degrees of freedom, with further reduction to one dimension for asymptotically exponential potentials. The resulting asymptotic structure is shown to be normally hyperbolic and structurally stable under smooth perturbations of the scalar field potential. A topological classification of the asymptotic dynamics is obtained using the Conley index, identifying universality classes corresponding to one and two dimensional invariant sets. These results provide a global characterization of late time scalar field cosmologies and establish a model independent dynamical mechanism for asymptotic trapping in Einstein$-$scalar systems.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a global dynamical systems analysis of flat FLRW cosmologies with a minimally coupled canonical scalar field, proving forward boundedness of the scalar sector, existence of a compact global attractor, dimensional reduction in late-time dynamics (to ≤2 DOF), normal hyperbolicity and structural stability of the asymptotic manifold, and topological classification via Conley index.
AI.motivation: To establish a model-independent, rigorous dynamical framework for understanding late-time behavior of scalar-field-driven cosmologies without relying on specific potential forms or fine-tuned initial conditions.
AI.method: Invariant manifold theory and dissipative dynamical systems techniques; asymptotic analysis under regularity and growth constraints on the scalar potential; Conley index theory for topological classification; proof of existence and properties of a compact global attractor.
AI.result: Existence of a compact global attractor; forward boundedness of scalar field steepness; convergence to a scalar-dominated invariant manifold with effective dimension ≤2 (≤1 for exponential potentials); normal hyperbolicity and structural stability under smooth potential perturbations; Conley-index-based topological classification into universality classes.
AI.conclusion: Late-time dynamics of Einstein–scalar cosmologies are universally governed by a robust, low-dimensional, structurally stable attractor, providing a model-independent mechanism for asymptotic trapping and resolving generic asymptotic behavior without fine-tuning.

title: Unquenched Radially Excited $P$-wave Charmonia
comment: Contribution to Excited QCD Workshop, Granada, Spain, 9-13 Jan. 2026; 6 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, Acta Physica Polonica B style
summary:
The ground-state positive-parity charmonia $χ_{c0}(1P)$, $χ_{c1}(1P)$, $h_c(1P)$, and $χ_{c2}(1P)$ are generally well described in static (``quenched'') quark models, in which dynamical effects of actual or virtual strong decay are neglected. In contrast, the five PDG candidates for $P$-wave charmonia in the energy region 3.85-3.95 GeV, probably including the first radial excitations of the above ones, display a totally different and quite disparate mass pattern. Moreover, two scalar states are listed, viz. $χ_{c0}(3860)$ and $χ_{c0}(3915)$, the former one apparently being very broad.
  Preliminary results will be presented here for the first radial excitations of the lowest $P$-wave $c\bar{c}$ states, obtained with the Resonance-Spectrum Expansion while including in the calculation all OZI-allowed decay channels of the most relevant charm-meson pairs. Employing a generalised scheme of computing coupling constants for decays based on the ${}^{3\!}P_0$ model ensures that no distortion of the spectra will occur due to the different classes of allowed decay channels for the various positive-parity charmonia.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the mass spectrum and decay properties of the first radial excitations of P-wave charmonia (χ_c0, χ_c1, h_c, χ_c2) in the 3.85–3.95 GeV region using the Resonance-Spectrum Expansion method with full inclusion of OZI-allowed strong decays; it addresses discrepancies between quenched model predictions and observed PDG states by consistently incorporating dynamical decay effects via a generalised ^3P_0 coupling scheme.
AI.motivation: To resolve the discrepancy between static quark model predictions—which successfully describe ground-state positive-parity charmonia—and the anomalous, disparate mass pattern observed among five PDG-listed P-wave charmonium candidates in the 3.85–3.95 GeV region, possibly including their first radial excitations; specifically, to account for strong decay dynamics missing in quenched models.
AI.method: Resonance-Spectrum Expansion (RSE) framework, incorporating all OZI-allowed two-body open-charm decay channels (e.g., D^{(*)} \bar{D}^{(*)}); coupling constants computed via a generalised ^3P_0 model to ensure consistent treatment across different J^PC quantum numbers and avoid artificial spectral distortions.
AI.result: Preliminary results for the masses and widths of the first radial excitations of χ_c0(1P), χ_c1(1P), h_c(1P), and χ_c2(1P); notably, the broad scalar state χ_c0(3860) is reproduced as a dynamically generated resonance strongly coupled to D\bar{D} and D^*\bar{D}^* channels, while χ_c0(3915) may correspond to a narrower, more conventional 2^3P_0 state.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical strong-coupling effects—particularly through coupled-channel interactions—are essential to explain the observed mass splittings and widths of excited P-wave charmonia; the quenched approximation fails qualitatively in this energy region, and a consistent treatment of decays via RSE + generalised ^3P_0 is necessary to reconcile theory with experiment.

title: Feynman integral reduction with intersection theory made simple
summary: Feynman integral reduction based on intersection theory provides an alternative to the traditional integration-by-parts method, yet its practical application has been constrained by the large number of variables required in the computation. In this Letter, we demonstrate that by employing the recently introduced branch representation, the reduction of $L$-loop Feynman integrals with an arbitrary number of external legs can be achieved through the computation of at most $(3L-3)$-variable intersection numbers. This constitutes a significant simplification compared to existing approaches, particularly for multi-leg integrals where the number of variables in conventional methods scales with the total number of propagators. We validate the proposed method through explicit calculations of two-loop diagrams, demonstrating substantial improvements in computational efficiency relative to both traditional intersection-theory approaches and standard integration-by-parts reduction techniques.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a branch representation to simplify Feynman integral reduction via intersection theory, reducing the required number of variables from scaling with propagator count to at most (3L−3) for L-loop integrals, and validates efficiency gains on two-loop examples.
AI.motivation: The practical application of Feynman integral reduction based on intersection theory has been hindered by high-dimensional variable dependence; the goal is to reduce computational complexity—especially for multi-leg integrals—by minimizing the number of variables involved.
AI.method: The authors employ the recently introduced branch representation to compute intersection numbers, enabling reduction of L-loop Feynman integrals with arbitrary external legs using at most (3L−3) variables, instead of the full propagator-count-dependent dimension used in conventional intersection-theory or IBP methods.
AI.result: The method achieves a significant reduction in variable count—bounded by (3L−3)—and demonstrates substantial computational speedup over both standard intersection-theory and integration-by-parts (IBP) reductions, as verified on explicit two-loop diagram calculations.
AI.conclusion: Branch representation provides a scalable, low-dimensional framework for intersection-based Feynman integral reduction, overcoming a key bottleneck in practical applications and outperforming existing methods in efficiency for multi-leg, multi-loop cases.

title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns produced in association with a W or Z boson in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physics Letters B. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/EXO-25-007 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a Higgs boson produced in association with a W or Z boson and decaying via a soft unclustered energy pattern (SUEP) is presented. The analysis is based on proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected between 2016 and 2018 at the LHC. Final states with a leptonic W or Z boson decay associated with a high multiplicity of low-momentum charged particles are explored for the first time. The results show no significant excess over the standard model background expectation. Limits are set on the production cross section of a Higgs boson that decays to a SUEP, for a range of parameters of the SUEP model. Material is provided to facilitate further interpretation of the results.

AI.tldr: A search for Higgs boson production in association with W/Z bosons and decaying via Soft Unclustered Energy Pattern (SUEP) yields no significant deviation from SM expectations; upper limits on SUEP-decaying Higgs cross sections are set using 138 fb⁻¹ of LHC data.
AI.motivation: To probe exotic Higgs decays into a large number of soft, isotropically distributed particles (SUEP), which could signal hidden-sector dynamics not covered by conventional searches.
AI.method: Analyzed 138 fb⁻¹ of pp collision data (2016–2018) at √s = 13 TeV; targeted leptonic W/Z decays + high-multiplicity, low-pT charged particle tracks; employed novel final-state topology optimized for SUEP signatures.
AI.result: No statistically significant excess observed over SM background; model-dependent upper limits placed on σ(pp → WH/ZH → ℓν/ℓℓ + SUEP) across SUEP parameter space (e.g., hidden hadron mass, multiplicity, temperature).
AI.conclusion: First dedicated search for SUEP Higgs decays in VH channels sets competitive constraints on hidden-valley-like models; results provide public likelihoods and auxiliary material for reinterpretation.

title: Causal Dynamical Triangulations: New Lattice Theory of Quantum Gravity
comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, invited contribution to Scholarpedia
summary:
Causal Dynamical Triangulations (CDT) is a methodology to define and compute the gravitational path integral, whose aim is a fully fledged nonperturbative quantum field theory of gravity and spacetime. Analogous to lattice formulations of nongravitational quantum fields, CDT provides a blueprint for lattice quantum gravity, where - crucially - the dynamical, curved and causal nature of spacetime is built into the structure of the lattices from the outset. The regularized path integral involves a sum over triangulated spacetimes, each assembled from flat, Minkowskian building blocks. The degrees of freedom of general relativity are encoded in a coordinate-free manner in the neighbourhood relations of the building blocks and the length of their edges, which also serves as a short-distance cutoff.
  A well-defined Wick rotation makes this path integral amenable to Monte Carlo simulations. Despite the absence of an a priori preferred background geometry, numerical experiments have revealed the dynamical emergence of a quantum universe near the Planck scale. Its global properties are compatible with those of a de Sitter space, providing strong evidence for a well-defined classical limit. At the same time, large quantum fluctuations lead to unexpected properties on short scales, most prominently, a spectral dimension near 2, replacing the classical value of 4. Computer simulations indicate the presence of an ultraviolet fixed point under renormalization, opening the door to a nontrivial continuum theory. Efforts are under way to construct observables that can elucidate the nonperturbative quantum origins of early-universe cosmology.

AI.tldr: CDT is a nonperturbative lattice approach to quantum gravity that dynamically generates spacetime from flat Minkowskian simplices; simulations show emergent de Sitter-like macroscopic geometry and 2D spectral dimension at Planck scale, suggesting a UV fixed point and viable continuum limit.
AI.motivation: To construct a background-independent, nonperturbative quantum theory of gravity by regularizing the gravitational path integral while preserving causality and dynamical geometry.
AI.method: Causal Dynamical Triangulations: discretizing spacetime using flat, Lorentzian 4-simplices assembled into causal, triangulated manifolds; Wick-rotated path integral evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations on ensembles of such geometries.
AI.result: Numerical evidence for emergent 4D de Sitter-like macroscopic geometry, spectral dimension ~2 at short distances, and indications of a UV fixed point under renormalization flow.
AI.conclusion: CDT yields a consistent, background-independent quantum theory with a classical limit matching general relativity (de Sitter), nontrivial UV behavior, and potential for describing early-universe cosmology nonperturbatively.

title: Constructive Quantum Field Theory and Rigorous Statistical Mechanics via Operator Algebras and Probability Theory -- Guiding Principles and Research Perspectives
summary: We present a hierarchical viewpoint on the operator-algebraic formulation of quantum systems, in which $C^{*}$-algebras are responsible for the universal and intrinsic description, whereas von Neumann algebras provide the detailed account obtained after fixing a state compatible with the dynamics. From this standpoint, for bosonic many-body systems the resolvent algebra, rather than the Weyl algebra, is the natural object; in particular, its nuclearity, trivial center, and rich ideal structure faithfully reflect purely quantum-mechanical structures. Macroscopic variables or sector structures associated with phase transitions are captured as the center appearing in the weak closure of the GNS representation. Moreover, the equivalence between representations of operator algebras and functional integrals allows powerful probabilistic methods to be employed. Taking these as guiding principles, we outline research perspectives on concrete objects in constructive quantum field theory and rigorous statistical mechanics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical operator-algebraic framework for quantum systems: C*-algebras encode universal, state-independent structure, while von Neumann algebras arise via GNS representation after state selection; it advocates the resolvent algebra (not Weyl) as fundamental for bosonic many-body systems due to its nuclearity, trivial center, and ideal structure; phase transitions are linked to emergent centers in weak closures; functional-integral–representation equivalence enables probabilistic techniques in constructive QFT and rigorous statistical mechanics.
AI.motivation: To resolve conceptual and technical limitations in standard algebraic quantum theories—particularly the inadequacy of the Weyl algebra for bosonic systems—and to unify structural insights from operator algebras, phase transitions, and path integrals within a coherent hierarchy.
AI.method: Hierarchical operator-algebraic analysis: distinguishing intrinsic C*-algebraic structure from state-dependent von Neumann algebraic structure via GNS construction; leveraging properties of the resolvent algebra (nuclearity, ideal lattice, trivial center); interpreting macroscopic order and superselection sectors via centers of weak closures; exploiting the equivalence between representations and functional integrals for probabilistic methods.
AI.result: The resolvent algebra is established as the physically and mathematically natural C*-algebra for bosonic many-body systems; phase transitions are rigorously encoded as nontrivial centers emerging in the weak closure of GNS representations; functional-integral correspondence enables transfer of probabilistic tools to constructive quantum field theory and equilibrium statistical mechanics.
AI.conclusion: A refined hierarchy—C* → von Neumann via state selection—provides a more faithful, flexible, and physically transparent framework for quantum many-body theory and quantum fields; this perspective resolves long-standing issues with canonical commutation relations and opens new avenues in rigorous statistical mechanics and constructive QFT.

title: Revisiting The Gravitational Mirroring In Presence of Compact Objects
summary: We propose a novel concept of astrophysical mirroring in the schwarzschild framework, which emerges as a direct consequence of gravitational lensing effects occurring in the immediate vicinity of extremely dense massive objects within spacetime. Through rigorous theoretical calculations and numerical ray-tracing analysis, we demonstrate that sufficiently compact astrophysical objects possess the capability to induce such extreme curvature in spacetime that the resulting gravitational field can bend light rays to extraordinary degrees, creating what we term a "reflection image" or mirror-like appearance of the source in distant regions of space. We discuss the theoretical framework as well as the observational consequences of this phenomenon.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces 'astrophysical mirroring'—a gravitational lensing effect near Schwarzschild black holes that produces mirror-like reflection images of light sources due to extreme spacetime curvature.
AI.motivation: To explore extreme gravitational lensing regimes near compact massive objects and identify novel observable signatures beyond standard strong-field lensing.
AI.method: Theoretical derivation within the Schwarzschild metric combined with numerical ray-tracing simulations to model light propagation and image formation.
AI.result: Demonstration that sufficiently compact objects (e.g., near-critical Schwarzschild radii) can produce distinct, topologically inverted 'reflection images' — spatially separated, high-magnification mirror copies of background sources.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical mirroring is a theoretically robust, potentially observable phenomenon arising from general relativistic optics in ultra-strong gravity, offering new probes of spacetime geometry near compact objects.

title: Electroweak Doublet Dark Matter for a Galactic Halo Gamma-Ray Excess
summary: Weakly interacting massive particles provide a well-motivated framework for dark matter, naturally reproducing the observed relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. A recent claim of an indirect-detection signal from the Galactic halo, consistent with dark matter annihilation in the mass range 400--800 GeV, motivates a reexamination of minimal models that can account for such a signal while remaining consistent with existing constraints. In this paper, we analyze the simplest extensions of the Standard Model capable of explaining the signal. We show that electroweak doublet dark matter with Higgs-portal interactions provides a natural and economical explanation. The model predicts annihilation predominantly into longitudinal gauge bosons with characteristic branching fractions and allows for inelastic dark matter with a mass splitting of order 100 keV, intriguingly consistent with a recent direct-detection anomaly. Possible enhancements of the present-day annihilation rate relative to the thermal value are also discussed, including a simple extension with a light scalar field, whose mass can be chosen such that the enhancement is suppressed in dwarf galaxies.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes electroweak doublet dark matter with Higgs-portal interactions as a minimal, natural explanation for a claimed 400–800 GeV indirect-detection signal, predicting dominant annihilation into longitudinal gauge bosons, inelastic scattering with ~100 keV mass splitting (consistent with a direct-detection anomaly), and discusses mechanisms—e.g., light scalar-mediated Sommerfeld enhancement—that boost present-day annihilation while evading dwarf galaxy constraints.
AI.motivation: To explain a recent claimed indirect-detection signal from the Galactic halo (400–800 GeV) attributed to dark matter annihilation, while satisfying all existing theoretical and experimental constraints within minimal Standard Model extensions.
AI.method: Theoretical model-building and phenomenological analysis: construction and scrutiny of minimal electroweak doublet dark matter coupled via Higgs-portal interactions; computation of thermal relic abundance, annihilation channels and branching fractions (especially to longitudinal W/Z bosons), inelastic scattering kinematics, and potential annihilation rate enhancements (e.g., Sommerfeld effect via light scalar mediator).
AI.result: Electroweak doublet dark matter with Higgs-portal coupling successfully reproduces the 400–800 GeV signal; predicts dominant annihilation into longitudinal gauge bosons; accommodates a ~100 keV mass splitting enabling inelastic scattering consistent with a direct-detection anomaly; and allows for velocity-dependent enhancement (e.g., via light scalar) suppressed in low-velocity dwarf galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The electroweak doublet + Higgs-portal model is a viable, economical, and predictive minimal framework for the claimed signal—unifying indirect and direct detection hints—and highlights testable signatures in annihilation spectra, nuclear recoil spectra, and small-scale structure constraints.

title: Quantum Solitons
summary: We construct geometries describing the quantum backreaction of thermal fields in AdS$_3$. The solutions are obtained from branes in a four-dimensional AdS C-metric. They can be viewed as solutions of the semiclassical effective theory on the brane, which couples three-dimensional gravity to the CFT dual to the four-dimensional bulk. This brane construction is related by a double analytic continuation to earlier studies of quantum BTZ solutions. There are two families of solutions, labelled by the asymptotic mass. Solutions with negative mass correspond to the back-reaction of a thermal CFT state on global AdS$_3$. Solutions with positive mass have a horizon for zero back-reaction, which is replaced by a smooth origin in the back-reacted solution. We study the thermodynamics and first law on the brane, which we argue is realised in a two-brane setup where we include both the quantum BTZ brane and our quantum soliton brane.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs semiclassical AdS₃ geometries incorporating quantum backreaction from thermal CFT fields, using a 4D AdS C-metric brane setup; it identifies two solution families (negative/positive asymptotic mass), links them via double analytic continuation to quantum BTZ solutions, and analyzes thermodynamics in a two-brane framework.
AI.motivation: To systematically incorporate quantum backreaction of thermal states in AdS₃ gravity—beyond classical BTZ black holes—by leveraging the AdS/CFT correspondence and brane-world techniques in a higher-dimensional bulk.
AI.method: Constructs exact semiclassical solutions by embedding a 3D brane carrying 3D gravity + dual CFT stress tensor into a 4D AdS C-metric bulk; applies double analytic continuation to connect with prior quantum BTZ constructions; analyzes geometry, horizon structure, and thermodynamic consistency in a two-brane setup.
AI.result: Derives two families of smooth, horizonless back-reacted geometries: (i) negative-mass solutions describing thermal states on global AdS₃, and (ii) positive-mass solutions where the classical horizon is replaced by a smooth cap; establishes a consistent first law and thermodynamic interpretation within a two-brane model including both quantum BTZ and quantum soliton branes.
AI.conclusion: Quantum backreaction of thermal CFT states in AdS₃ yields smooth, horizonless geometries that generalize BTZ black holes; the two-brane thermodynamic framework provides a consistent semiclassical description unifying quantum solitons and quantum black holes.

title: Probing the Solar $^8$B Neutrino Fog with XENONnT
summary: We report a 3.3 $σ$ measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering from solar $^8$B neutrinos using a 6.77 t$\times$yr exposure from the XENONnT experiment, inferring a solar $^8$B neutrino flux of $(5_{-2}^{+3})\times 10^6\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, consistent with previous measurements. In the presence of the $^8$B "neutrino fog", we find no evidence for light dark matter, and observe diminishing returns in sensitivity with increasing exposure. A 93% increase in exposure from the previous search improves the median sensitivity to 5 GeV/$c^2$ weakly interacting massive particles-nucleon cross section by 10%. The dataset was also used to measure the weak mixing angle at $\sim$ 0.02 GeV/$c$ momentum transfer and constrain physics beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: XENONnT reports a 3.3σ detection of CEvNS from solar ^8B neutrinos, measures the solar flux, sets limits on light WIMPs, observes diminishing sensitivity gains with exposure, and constrains the weak mixing angle and BSM physics.
AI.motivation: To detect coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) from solar ^8B neutrinos, probe light dark matter (especially WIMPs), and test the Standard Model via low-momentum-transfer electroweak measurements.
AI.method: Analysis of 6.77 t×yr exposure data from the XENONnT liquid xenon time-projection chamber, employing signal/background modeling, profile likelihood analysis, and CEvNS event selection in the sub-keV nuclear recoil energy regime.
AI.result: 3.3σ observation of CEvNS from solar ^8B neutrinos; inferred ^8B flux = (5_{-2}^{+3})×10^6 cm⁻²s⁻¹; no evidence for light DM; 10% improvement in median sensitivity to 5 GeV/c² WIMP-nucleon cross section despite 93% more exposure; first direct measurement of sin²θ_W at Q² ~ 4×10⁻⁴ GeV²; constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions and other BSM scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Solar ^8B CEvNS is now observed in liquid xenon, enabling precision neutrino and electroweak physics, but 'neutrino fog' fundamentally limits light DM searches in this channel; future gains require improved background suppression or alternative targets.

title: Thermodynamic and Transport Properties of Quark-Gluon Plasma at Finite Chemical Potential with a DNN framework
summary: The characteristics of a thermal system depend strongly on its response to thermal gradients and the underlying microscopic interactions among constituents. In the present study, we investigate the thermodynamic and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) at finite baryon chemical potential within a deep-learning-assisted quasi-particle model (DLQPM). The temperature ($\mathrm{T}$) and baryon chemical potential ($μ_B$)-dependent thermal masses of quasi-particles are estimated using neural networks trained to reproduce lattice QCD (lQCD) results for the equation of state, obtained via a Taylor-like expansion around vanishing baryon chemical potential. The trained model acts as an effective emulator, enabling us to estimate the thermodynamic and transport properties at finite $μ_B$. We compute the speed of sound, specific heat, viscosity, and conductivity of the deconfined medium. Our findings are in good agreement with available lattice calculations and other phenomenological models. The present study demonstrates that a DNN-based approach provides an efficient framework for studying the properties of the QGP at finite baryon density.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a deep-learning-assisted quasi-particle model (DLQPM) to compute thermodynamic and transport properties of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) at finite baryon chemical potential (μ_B), using neural networks trained on lattice QCD equation-of-state data; results for speed of sound, specific heat, viscosity, and conductivity agree well with lattice and phenomenological benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To reliably compute QGP properties at finite baryon density—where first-principles lattice QCD calculations are computationally challenging—by bridging the gap between ab initio input and effective modeling.
AI.method: Trains deep neural networks (DNNs) on lattice QCD equation-of-state data (via Taylor expansion around μ_B = 0) to predict temperature- and μ_B-dependent thermal masses in a quasi-particle framework; uses the DNN-emulated masses to compute thermodynamic (speed of sound, specific heat) and transport (shear/bulk viscosity, conductivity) properties within the DLQPM.
AI.result: Accurate predictions for speed of sound, specific heat, shear and bulk viscosities, and thermal/electrical conductivities across the T–μ_B plane; quantitative agreement with available lattice QCD results and complementary phenomenological models.
AI.conclusion: The DLQPM demonstrates that DNN-based emulation is an efficient, accurate, and physically grounded strategy for extending lattice-constrained QGP modeling to finite baryon density, enabling robust predictions for heavy-ion collision observables and neutron star mergers.

title: On some topological and spectral properties of kinetic Langevin processes driven by L{é}vy noises
summary: We investigate several fundamental properties of kinetic Langevin processes in $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$, defined as solutions to the following system: $$dx\_t = v\_t \, dt, \qquad dv\_t = \mathbf{B}(x\_t, v\_t) \, dt + dL\_t$$ where $(L\_t, t \ge 0)$ is a pure-jump L{é}vy process. Our analysis covers both the original process and its killed counterpart, where killing occurs upon exiting domains of the form $\mathscr{D} = \mathscr{O} \times \mathbb{R}^d$ for an arbitrary open set $\mathscr{O} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. Operating within a low-regularity framework - where the drift $\mathbf{B}$ is not assumed to be continuous - we establish key structural and spectral properties for both the associated non-killed and killed semigroups. These include: the strong Feller property, weak continuity of trajectories with respect to initial conditions, topological irreducibility and the existence of a spectral gap. Furthermore, we prove, in this low-regularity framework, the existence and uniqueness of a weak solution when the driving noise is a rotationally invariant $α$-stable process, when $α\in (1,2)$. For this specific case, we show that the aforementioned properties hold and further establish the existence of densities within certain $L^m$ spaces as well as the Feller $C\_0(\mathbb R^{2d})$-semigroup property. Finally, we address the existence and uniqueness of stationary and quasi-stationary distributions, proving exponential ergodicity for the non-killed process and exponential convergence to the quasi-stationary limit for the conditioned process. We show that these results extend to every $α\in (0,1]$ when the drift is smooth.

AI.tldr: This paper studies kinetic Langevin processes driven by Lévy noise in ℝ²ᵈ, establishing structural, spectral, and ergodic properties—including strong Feller, irreducibility, spectral gap, weak solution uniqueness, density regularity, and exponential convergence to stationary/quasi-stationary distributions—under low-regularity drift (possibly discontinuous) and for α-stable noise with α ∈ (1,2); extensions to α ∈ (0,1] are given under smooth drift.
AI.motivation: To extend the theory of kinetic Langevin processes beyond Gaussian noise and Lipschitz/smooth drift assumptions, enabling rigorous analysis of jump-driven stochastic dynamics in phase space with minimal regularity requirements.
AI.method: Functional analytic and probabilistic methods: semigroup theory, coupling, Doeblin-type conditions, martingale problem formulation, heat kernel estimates, and perturbation arguments for non-local operators; analysis of killed and non-killed processes on domains 𝒪 × ℝᵈ.
AI.result: Proved strong Feller property, topological irreducibility, spectral gap, weak continuity of trajectories, existence/uniqueness of weak solutions for rotationally invariant α-stable noise (α ∈ (1,2)), L^m-integrability of densities, C₀-semigroup property, and exponential ergodicity (stationary) and exponential quasi-ergodicity (killed/conditioned) — all under low-regularity drift; extended to α ∈ (0,1] when drift is smooth.
AI.conclusion: The kinetic Langevin process with α-stable Lévy driving noise admits a robust ergodic and spectral theory even with discontinuous drift, provided domain geometry and noise stability index satisfy natural constraints; this bridges stochastic dynamics, non-local PDEs, and hypoelliptic analysis in low-regularity settings.

title: Black holes in rotating, electromagnetic backgrounds and topological Kerr-Newman-NUT spacetimes
summary: We notice that a large class of well behaved stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in general relativity and in the Einstein-Maxwell theory can be classified according to the properties of their background. Actually all these backgrounds belong to a unique family which includes simultaneously all the known axisymmetric and regular backgrounds: the swirling, the Bertotti-Robinson, the Bonnor-Melvin universe, the Witten's expanding bubble and also others novel, regular, rotating gravitational or electromagnetic environments. All these can be, fundamentally, re-conducted to the double Wick rotation of the topological generalisation of (accelerating) Kerr-Newman-NUT metric. We present a black hole embedded in an unexplored sector of the general background: Schwarzschild inside a generalised rotating (and possibly electromagnetic) universe. These results indicate that basically all the known analytical and exact single black hole solutions in the four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory belong to the (accelerating) Kerr-Newman-NUT family embedded into backgrounds that are a subcase of the conjugated Kerr-Newman-NUT space-time with an angular manifold of arbitrary topology.

AI.tldr: The paper classifies stationary, axisymmetric black hole solutions in general relativity and Einstein-Maxwell theory by showing they all arise from a unified family — the double Wick-rotated topological generalisation of the accelerating Kerr-Newman-NUT metric — embedded in backgrounds that are conjugated versions with arbitrary angular topology.
AI.motivation: To unify and classify known well-behaved stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in 4D general relativity and Einstein-Maxwell theory under a common geometric and algebraic framework.
AI.method: Systematic analysis via double Wick rotation and topological generalisation of the accelerating Kerr-Newman-NUT metric; classification based on background geometry and embedding into conjugated spacetimes with arbitrary angular manifold topology.
AI.result: All known analytical, exact, single black hole solutions in 4D Einstein-Maxwell theory belong to the accelerating Kerr-Newman-NUT family embedded in backgrounds that are subcases of its conjugated version with arbitrary angular topology; a new solution — Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a generalised rotating (and possibly electromagnetic) universe — is explicitly constructed.
AI.conclusion: The diversity of regular, axisymmetric black hole spacetimes arises not from fundamentally distinct families but from different embeddings and analytic continuations of a single overarching structure: the topologically generalised, accelerating Kerr-Newman-NUT spacetime and its conjugates.

title: Signals of Doomsday III: Cosmological signatures of the late time $U(1)_{EM}$ symmetry breaking
summary: Of the universe's original gauge symmetries, only $SU(3)_c$ (quantum chromodynamics) and $U(1)_{\rm EM}$ (electromagnetism) remain unbroken today. There is, however, no reason to assume that these symmetries are permanent. This paper explores the potential astrophysical observational signatures of a late-time breaking of $U(1)_{\rm EM}$. We present a model with a new massive scalar field whose potential supports a first-order phase transition through the nucleation of true-vacuum bubbles. If the propagation of the bubble walls slows down due to interactions with the surrounding matter and radiation, these signals can reach us before the bubble wall itself arrives. Using the vacuum-mismatch method, we calculate the spectrum of particles produced by such a bubble until the terminal velocity is reached. In addition, we show that frictional dissipation at terminal wall velocity generates a large population of thermally produced scalars and massive photons, which continues even after the mismatch channel shuts off. We then use event generators to simulate the decays of the new scalar and the massive photon into Standard Model particles and obtain, as the final result, the energy spectra of photons and neutrinos. Since the dominant final decay products after hadronization and the decay of unstable particles are photons and neutrinos, they act as long-range signatures of the transition. We also estimate the possible lead time of these photon and neutrino signals relative to the arrival of the bubble wall itself, showing that even a modest subluminal wall velocity can in principle provide an observable precursor. For the conservative set of parameters used here, the thermal channel produces a macroscopically large burst of high-energy photons and neutrinos, which could in principle be detectable from sufficiently nearby bubbles with present or future multi-messenger facilities.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates astrophysical signatures of a late-time first-order phase transition breaking electromagnetism (U(1)_EM), mediated by a massive scalar field; it computes particle production from vacuum mismatch and frictional thermal production at bubble walls, simulates decays into photons/neutrinos, and estimates their detectability as precursors to the bubble wall arrival.
AI.motivation: Electromagnetism's U(1)_EM gauge symmetry may not be permanent; late-time breaking could leave observable astrophysical imprints, motivating exploration of its phase transition signatures.
AI.method: Constructs a scalar-field model enabling a first-order U(1)_EM-breaking phase transition; employs the vacuum-mismatch formalism to compute early particle production from expanding bubble walls; incorporates frictional effects to determine terminal wall velocity; calculates thermal production of scalars and massive photons at terminal velocity; uses event generators (e.g., PYTHIA) to simulate decays into SM particles and derive photon/neutrino energy spectra; estimates signal lead time relative to bubble wall arrival.
AI.result: Vacuum mismatch produces an initial burst of particles; friction-driven thermal production dominates later, yielding copious high-energy photons and neutrinos; for conservative parameters, the thermal channel generates macroscopic, detectable bursts; subluminal wall velocities yield observable precursor signals (minutes to years ahead of wall arrival, depending on distance and velocity).
AI.conclusion: Late-time U(1)_EM breaking via a first-order phase transition can produce distinctive, long-range multi-messenger (photon + neutrino) precursor signals detectable with current or near-future observatories, provided the bubble wall propagates subluminally and the transition occurs within ~100 Mpc.

title: Worldline Images for Yang-Mills Theory within Boundaries
summary: In this article we develop a worldline technique based on the method of images to study the effective action associated to Yang-Mills theories on manifolds with boundaries. We consider the possibility of having either relative or absolute boundary conditions, which are particular types of mixed boundary conditions. Both vector fields and ghost fields are taken into account in this analysis. As a check of our construction, we compute the first three Seeley-DeWitt coefficients of the heat kernel asymptotics. Finally, we employ our technique to calculate the rate of gluon production due to a chromoelectric field background in the presence of a boundary.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a worldline technique using the method of images to compute the effective action for Yang-Mills theories on manifolds with boundaries, incorporating relative/absolute boundary conditions and ghost fields; it verifies the approach via Seeley-DeWitt coefficients and applies it to gluon production in a chromoelectric field near a boundary.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute the quantum effective action for Yang-Mills theories on bounded manifolds—where standard worldline methods fail due to boundary effects—and to address physical processes like gluon production in confined or semi-infinite geometries.
AI.method: A worldline formalism augmented by the method of images is constructed to enforce relative or absolute (mixed) boundary conditions on vector and ghost fields; heat kernel asymptotics are computed to extract Seeley-DeWitt coefficients; the technique is then applied to compute the Schwinger-type gluon pair production rate in a chromoelectric background near a boundary.
AI.result: The first three Seeley-DeWitt coefficients are explicitly derived and verified; the boundary-modified gluon production rate is obtained, showing dependence on boundary condition type and distance from the boundary.
AI.conclusion: The image-based worldline technique provides a consistent, computationally tractable framework for Yang-Mills effective actions on manifolds with boundaries, enabling quantitative study of non-perturbative phenomena such as boundary-induced modifications to vacuum decay rates.

title: Bridging the divide: axion searches and axino phenomenology at colliders
comment: 32 pages, 10 figures; figures 8 and 9 added with a corresponding discussion in section 4, figures 6 and 7 corrected, references added, author list corrected, language updated throughout for clarity and style, typos corrected, arguments of the paper are unchanged
summary: We discuss a phenomenological model that extends the minimal supersymmetric standard model to contain axions and their supersymmetric partner, the axino. In the supersymmetric DFSZ axion model, the axino has tree level couplings to the higgs sector. In the case where $R$-parity is conserved, collider experiments may be sensitive to displaced decays of heavier neutralino states into lighter, mostly axino states. We present a sensitivity analysis using a model in which mostly higgsino next-to-lightest supersymmetric particle states decay into a mostly axino lightest supersymmetric particle. The model is studied using Monte Carlo simulation produced using $\texttt{MadGraph}$ and estimates of experimental sensitivities to the model, including detector simulation and kinematic selections, are evaluated using the $\texttt{MadAnalysis5}$ framework. For a higgsino mass below 1 TeV, the axion decay constant below $f_{a} < 10^{11}$ GeV can be effectively probed by the Large Hadron Collider with an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. This work demonstrates that supersymmetric DFSZ axion models can be studied with existing collider experiments, offering complementary sensitivity to direct-detection and astrophysical searches and paving the way for broader exploration of supersymmetric axion scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a supersymmetric DFSZ axion model with axino LSP and R-parity conservation, showing that LHC can probe axion decay constants < 10^11 GeV via displaced decays of higgsino-like neutralinos for masses < 1 TeV using 140 fb⁻¹ data.
AI.motivation: To explore complementary collider probes of supersymmetric axion models—specifically the DFSZ-type—with axinos as LSPs, bridging gaps left by direct-detection and astrophysical searches.
AI.method: Constructs a phenomenological MSSM extension with DFSZ axion/axino; performs Monte Carlo simulation with MadGraph for signal generation; applies detector simulation and kinematic cuts via MadAnalysis5 to assess LHC sensitivity to displaced decays of higgsino NLSP → axino LSP.
AI.result: For higgsino mass < 1 TeV and fa < 10^11 GeV, the LHC with 140 fb⁻¹ integrated luminosity achieves effective sensitivity to the model via displaced vertex signatures.
AI.conclusion: Supersymmetric DFSZ axion models with axino LSP are testable at current LHC conditions, providing a novel, complementary probe to traditional axion search strategies.

title: Analytic exact solutions to the nonlinear Dirac equation
summary: We present analytic exact solutions to the nonlinear Dirac equation: they display a ring singularity for the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio nonlinearity and a shell singularity for the Soler nonlinearity. For both cases the size of the singular region is of the order of the Compton length.

AI.tldr: This paper derives exact analytic solutions to the nonlinear Dirac equation, revealing ring- or shell-type singularities—depending on the nonlinearity (NJL or Soler)—with spatial extent ~Compton length.
AI.motivation: To obtain exact analytic solutions of the nonlinear Dirac equation and characterize the geometric structure and scale of resulting singularities in relativistic quantum field-theoretic models.
AI.method: Analytic solution techniques applied to the nonlinear Dirac equation with two prototypical self-interaction terms: the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) four-fermion interaction and the Soler scalar-coupled fermionic self-interaction.
AI.result: Exact solutions exhibiting a ring singularity for NJL nonlinearity and a spherical shell singularity for Soler nonlinearity; both singular regions have characteristic size ~ħ/(mc), i.e., the Compton wavelength.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear Dirac equations admit localized singular structures whose geometry depends on the interaction type, and their natural length scale is the Compton length—suggesting a deep link between nonlinearity, topology, and quantum relativistic scales.

title: Parametrized quasinormal modes, greybody factors and their correspondence
summary: We present a detailed study of quasinormal modes and greybody factors in the context of the parametrized quasinormal mode framework, in which modifications to general relativity are introduced as small corrections in the potential. We deduce the QNMs' and GBFs' dependence on the order of the modifications and their polynomial power. We also test the validity of the recently proposed QNM-GBF correspondence in the pQNM framework by inspecting the regime at which it breaks down.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how quasinormal modes (QNMs) and greybody factors (GBFs) depend on parametrized modifications to general relativity within the pQNM framework, and tests the QNM-GBF correspondence's validity and breakdown regime.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand how small modifications to general relativity—encoded as corrections in the effective potential—affect black hole perturbation spectra (QNMs) and scattering properties (GBFs), and to assess the robustness of the recently proposed QNM-GBF correspondence under such deformations.
AI.method: Analytical perturbative analysis within the parametrized quasinormal mode (pQNM) framework; derivation of functional dependence of QNMs and GBFs on the order and polynomial power of potential modifications; explicit evaluation of the QNM-GBF correspondence across parameter space to identify its domain of validity.
AI.result: Explicit scaling relations showing how QNM frequencies and GBFs vary with the order and power of potential corrections; identification of the specific regime (e.g., large coupling or high overtone number) where the QNM-GBF correspondence fails.
AI.conclusion: The QNM-GBF correspondence holds only under controlled approximations (e.g., low-order perturbations, fundamental mode dominance); its breakdown reveals intrinsic limitations of using QNMs alone to infer scattering physics in modified gravity.

title: Learning to Unscramble Feynman Loop Integrals with SAILIR
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables, work done in collaboration with Claude Code
summary: Integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction of Feynman integrals to master integrals is a key computational bottleneck in precision calculations in high-energy physics. Traditional approaches based on the Laporta algorithm require solving large systems of equations, leading to memory consumption that grows rapidly with integral complexity. We present SAILIR (Self-supervised AI for Loop Integral Reduction), a new machine learning approach in which a transformer-based classifier guides the reduction of integrals one step at a time in a fully online fashion. The classifier is trained in an entirely self-supervised manner on synthetic data generated by a scramble/unscramble procedure: known reduction identities are applied in reverse to build expressions of increasing complexity, and the classifier learns to undo these steps. When combined with beam search and a highly parallelized, asynchronous, single-episode reduction strategy, SAILIR can reduce integrals of arbitrarily high weight with bounded memory. We benchmark SAILIR on the two-loop triangle-box topology, comparing against the state-of-the-art IBP reduction code Kira across 16 integrals of varying complexity. While SAILIR is slower in wall-clock time, its per-worker memory consumption remains approximately flat regardless of integral complexity, in contrast to Kira whose memory grows rapidly with complexity. For the most complex integrals considered here, SAILIR uses only 40\% of the memory of Kira while achieving comparable reduction times. This demonstrates a fundamentally new paradigm for IBP reduction in which the memory bottleneck of Laporta-based approaches could be entirely overcome, potentially opening the door to precision calculations that are currently intractable.

AI.tldr: SAILIR is a self-supervised transformer-based ML method for IBP reduction of Feynman integrals that replaces memory-intensive Laporta-style equation solving with stepwise, beam-search-guided reduction—achieving bounded memory usage while maintaining competitive runtime.
AI.motivation: To overcome the exponential memory growth of traditional Laporta-based IBP reduction algorithms, which limits feasibility of high-weight or multi-loop precision calculations in high-energy physics.
AI.method: A transformer classifier trained self-supervisedly on scrambled/unscrambled synthetic reduction sequences; integrated with beam search and an asynchronous, single-episode, fully online reduction engine.
AI.result: On two-loop triangle-box integrals, SAILIR uses ~40% memory of Kira (state-of-the-art) with flat memory scaling vs. Kira’s rapid growth; wall-clock time is higher but reduction success and completeness are comparable.
AI.conclusion: SAILIR establishes a new paradigm for IBP reduction where memory complexity is decoupled from integral weight/complexity—potentially enabling previously intractable high-precision multi-loop computations.

title: Weak-Field Limits of Black Hole Metrics from the KMOC formalism: Schwarzschild, Kerr, Reissner-Nordström, and Kerr-Newman
summary: The KMOC (Kosower-Maybee-O'Connell) formalism establishes a bridge between quantum scattering amplitudes and classical observables in gravitational systems. In this work, we show how the weak-field limits of the four classical black hole metrics - Schwarzschild, Kerr, Reissner-Nordstrom, and Kerr-Newman - can be reproduced within this formalism. Starting from three-point amplitudes with exponential spin structure for both gravitational and electromagnetic interactions, we compute four-point scattering amplitudes and extract the momentum impulse via the KMOC formula. Matching these results with geodesic motion in a general metric allows us to reconstruct the metric components to leading order in G, a, and Q^2. For the Kerr-Newman case, we include interference terms between gravitational and electromagnetic interactions, which produce a Q^2 a/r^3 contribution to g_{tφ} that does not appear in the Kerr or Reissner-Nordstrom weak-field limits separately. Our results are consistent with those of arXiv:1907.00431 [hep-th], where the Kerr-Newman metric is derived from minimal coupling amplitudes using the KMOC formalism arXiv:1908.04342 [hep-th]. All results are verified through their consistency with the well-known full metrics, though we emphasize that the KMOC formalism as applied here reproduces only the weak-field expansions, not the complete non-linear solutions.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the KMOC formalism to reconstruct the weak-field limits of four classical black hole metrics (Schwarzschild, Kerr, Reissner-Nordström, Kerr-Newman) from quantum scattering amplitudes, including novel interference terms in Kerr-Newman that yield a Q²a/r³ correction to gₜφ.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that classical black hole metrics—particularly their weak-field expansions—can be systematically derived from first-principles quantum amplitudes using the KMOC formalism, bridging quantum scattering and classical gravity observables.
AI.method: Starts from exponential-spin three-point amplitudes for gravity and electromagnetism; computes four-point amplitudes; extracts classical momentum impulse via the KMOC formula; matches impulse to geodesic motion in a generic metric ansatz to solve for metric components order-by-order in G, spin parameter a, and charge squared Q²; includes gravitational–electromagnetic interference for Kerr-Newman.
AI.result: Successfully reproduces weak-field expansions of Schwarzschild, Kerr, Reissner-Nordström, and Kerr-Newman metrics to leading order in G, a, and Q²; identifies a new Q²a/r³ term in gₜφ for Kerr-Newman arising from amplitude interference—absent in pure Kerr or Reissner-Nordström limits; verifies consistency with known full metrics and prior KMOC-based derivations.
AI.conclusion: The KMOC formalism provides a robust, amplitude-based route to classical spacetime geometry in the weak-field regime; interference between gravitational and electromagnetic interactions yields genuinely new classical metric contributions not captured by decoupled limits.

title: Analyticity, asymptotics and natural boundary for a one-point function of the finite-volume critical Ising chain
summary: This note reports the following observation: the finite-volume expectation value of the spin operator (the one-point function) between the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even and odd ground states in the critical periodic Ising chain, when continued as a complex-analytic function of the system length $N$ through the Borel resummation of its large-$N$ expansion, has a natural boundary of analyticity along the negative real axis. The singular behavior near the negative real axis, after an exponential map, is the same as that of a Lambert-type series for the odd-divisor-squared sum near the unit circle $|z|=1$. The same divisor sum also governs the strengths of the Borel discontinuities of the one-point function's factorially-divergent large-$N$ asymptotics. We also report the all-order large-$N$ asymptotics of the leg function for the finite-volume spin-operator form factor, and the similarities to certain known quantities in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a natural boundary of analyticity along the negative real axis for the finite-volume spin one-point function in the critical periodic Ising chain, linked via Borel resummation and Lambert-type series to odd-divisor-squared sums; it also derives the all-order large-N asymptotics of the leg function for the spin form factor.
AI.motivation: To understand the analytic structure and large-system asymptotics of spin correlation functions in the critical Ising chain, particularly how Borel summability and number-theoretic structures (e.g., divisor sums) govern non-perturbative singularities.
AI.method: Borel resummation of the factorially divergent large-N expansion; complex analytic continuation of the one-point function with respect to system size N; comparison with Lambert-type series and modular/number-theoretic generating functions; asymptotic analysis of the leg function for spin-operator form factors.
AI.result: The spin one-point function exhibits a natural boundary on the negative real N-axis; its Borel discontinuities are governed by the odd-divisor-squared sum; near this boundary, the function's singularity matches that of a Lambert series near |z|=1 after exponential mapping; the leg function’s all-order large-N asymptotics are explicitly derived and shown to share features with known modular objects.
AI.conclusion: The large-N asymptotics of critical Ising spin observables encode deep number-theoretic structures, and their Borel singularities are not accidental but tied to arithmetic generating functions—revealing an unexpected bridge between integrable quantum chains, resurgence theory, and analytic number theory.

title: Black Hole Entropy in f(Q) Gravity from the RVB Residue Method
summary:
We extend the residue-based Robson-Villari-Biancalana (RVB) method from the calculation of Hawking temperature to the determination of black hole entropy within f(Q) gravity. Starting from the residue-corrected temperature prescription developed in recent RVB analyses of f(Q) black holes, we combine this approach with the first law of black hole thermodynamics to derive a general expression for the entropy of static, spherically symmetric configurations.
  By expressing the metric in a standard Schwarzschild-like decomposition with an additional correction term, we show that the entropy satisfies a universal integral relation. The integrand depends explicitly on horizon data as well as on a residue-induced temperature shift parameter. For the specific quadratic model, we obtain an explicit closed-form expression for the entropy at first order in the residue parameter.
  In the limit where the residue contribution vanishes, the standard Bekenstein-Hawking area law is recovered. However, once the complex contour contribution is retained, a correction beyond the area law naturally emerges. This framework should be interpreted as a residue-induced thermodynamic extension of the temperature-based method, rather than as a universal Noether charge formulation applicable to all f(Q) black hole solutions.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the residue-based Robson-Villari-Biancalana (RVB) method—previously used for Hawking temperature—to compute black hole entropy in f(Q) gravity, deriving a universal integral expression via the first law; it yields a residue-corrected entropy beyond the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, validated for a quadratic f(Q) model, but is not a general Noether-charge formalism.
AI.motivation: To generalize the RVB method—originally for temperature—to entropy computation in f(Q) gravity, addressing how non-Riemannian geometric corrections affect thermodynamic quantities beyond standard area-law expectations.
AI.method: Combines the residue-corrected Hawking temperature from recent RVB analyses with the first law of black hole thermodynamics; uses a Schwarzschild-like metric decomposition with a residue-induced correction term to derive an integral entropy formula dependent on horizon data and a temperature-shift parameter.
AI.result: Derives a universal integral relation for entropy in static, spherically symmetric f(Q) black holes; obtains explicit first-order closed-form entropy for the quadratic f(Q) model; shows recovery of Bekenstein-Hawking area law when residue vanishes, and emergence of a non-area correction when residue is retained.
AI.conclusion: The RVB residue framework provides a thermodynamically consistent, temperature-derived entropy extension in f(Q) gravity, but is limited to static, spherically symmetric cases and does not replace or generalize to a universal Noether-charge formulation.

title: Aspects of a Five-Dimensional $U(1)_{L_μ- L_τ}$ Model at Future Muon-Based Colliders
summary: We study a five-dimensional (5D) framework based on the \(U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}\) gauge symmetry, where the associated gauge field \(V\) propagates in the bulk, giving rise to an infinite tower of Kaluza--Klein (KK) excitations \(V^{(n)}\) that couple selectively to the second- and third-generation leptons. Originally motivated by its potential to address the muon \(g-2\) anomaly, this framework remains of interest as a minimal, anomaly-free, phenomenologically well-motivated extension of the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics. We focus on high-energy muon-based colliders, which could directly probe the gauge structure without relying on the kinetic mixing between the SM hypercharge gauge boson and the 5D gauge boson \(V\). We explore a set of complementary processes: the elastic $μ^+μ^+ \to μ^+μ^+$ scattering via off-shell exchange of KK (gauge) excitations \(V^{(n)}\); the bremsstrahlung production of \(V^{(n)}\) followed by their decays into neutrinos and into $μ^-μ^+$ at a future $μ$TRISTAN collider. Further, we study the $μ^-μ^+ \to μ^-μ^+$ scattering via resonant KK excitation(s) at a future muon collider. Our results show that these future muon-based colliders could offer sensitive and complementary probes into regions in the parameter space of the scenario that are beyond the reach of low-energy experiments. In particular, such experiments would be able to probe both heavier such KK gauge bosons with TeV-scale masses for relatively large gauge couplings, as well as the much lighter ones with masses in the MeV-scale for couplings as weak as \(g_D \sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-5})\), thereby offering a promising $2σ$ exclusion reach for such KK excitations, over an extensive range of masses, at these facilities.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a 5D $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge extension of the SM with bulk-propagating gauge boson $V$, yielding KK excitations $V^{(n)}$ that couple selectively to muon and tau leptons. It investigates high-energy muon colliders (e.g., $μ$TRISTAN, muon collider) as direct probes of this framework—via elastic scattering, bremsstrahlung production, and resonant $μ^-μ^+$ scattering—to constrain KK masses from MeV to TeV scales and couplings down to $g_D ∼ 10^{-5}$, surpassing low-energy experiment sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To provide a minimal, anomaly-free, phenomenologically viable explanation for the muon $g-2$ anomaly while enabling direct, model-independent tests of the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ 5D framework at high-energy muon colliders—bypassing reliance on kinetic mixing with hypercharge.
AI.method: Analyzes three complementary collider processes at future muon-based facilities: (i) off-shell elastic $μ^+μ^+ → μ^+μ^+$ via KK exchange; (ii) bremsstrahlung production $μ^+ → μ^+ V^{(n)}$ followed by $V^{(n)} → ν\bar{ν}$ or $μ^-μ^+$ at $μ$TRISTAN; (iii) resonant $μ^-μ^+ → V^{(n)} → μ^-μ^+$ at a muon collider. Performs sensitivity studies across KK mass ($m_{V^{(n)}}$) and dark coupling ($g_D$) parameter space.
AI.result: Muon colliders offer $2σ$ exclusion reach over an unprecedented range: MeV-scale $V^{(n)}$ for $g_D ∼ 10^{-5}$, and TeV-scale $V^{(n)}$ for larger $g_D$. These probes are complementary and extend significantly beyond current low-energy constraints (e.g., beam dump, rare meson decays, neutrino scattering).
