AI.conclusion: High-energy muon colliders constitute uniquely powerful and complementary tools to test the 5D $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ framework—covering both light-weakly-coupled and heavy-strongly-coupled KK gauge bosons—thereby positioning them as critical facilities for probing BSM physics linked to lepton flavor anomalies.

title: Untwisting the double copy: the zeroth copy as an optical seed
summary: We present a historical optical foundation for stationary vacuum Kerr--Schild spacetimes on a flat background and interpret it in modern double-copy language. In this setting, a complex optical seed \(ρ=-θ-iω\), built from the expansion and signed twist of the Kerr--Schild congruence, is harmonic, while its inverse obeys an eikonal equation and reconstructs the congruence algebraically. Thus the local stationary geometry is organized by a single complex seed. In the overlap of the stationary Kerr--Schild and Petrov type--D Weyl double-copy framework, this seed furnishes a normalized representative of the zeroth-copy data, while its real part yields the Kerr--Schild profile and its gradient generates the single-copy gauge-field strength. The construction provides, without recourse to twistor methods, a spacetime realization of how a single complex seed builds the congruence, organizes the associated spacetime and gauge fields, and encodes the geometric content of the zeroth copy.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a historical optical foundation for stationary vacuum Kerr–Schild spacetimes on flat backgrounds and interprets it via the modern double-copy framework, using a single complex optical seed ρ = −θ − iω (built from expansion θ and signed twist ω) that is harmonic and encodes the full geometry, congruence, gauge field, and zeroth-copy data.
AI.motivation: To unify classical geometric optics of stationary Kerr–Schild spacetimes with the modern double-copy paradigm—specifically bridging the Petrov type-D Weyl double-copy and Kerr–Schild formalisms—without relying on twistor theory.
AI.method: Analyzes the geometric optics of null geodesic congruences in stationary vacuum Kerr–Schild spacetimes; identifies the complex seed ρ = −θ − iω as harmonic and shows its inverse satisfies the eikonal equation; algebraically reconstructs the congruence and derives the Kerr–Schild profile and gauge-field strength from Re(ρ) and ∇ρ; maps ρ to the normalized zeroth-copy datum in the Weyl double-copy framework.
AI.result: A single harmonic complex optical seed ρ fully determines the null congruence, stationary Kerr–Schild metric, associated single-copy gauge field (via ∇ρ), and zeroth-copy data—providing a unified, twistor-free spacetime realization of double-copy structure for type-D vacuum solutions.
AI.conclusion: The local geometry and field content of stationary vacuum Kerr–Schild spacetimes are completely organized by one complex harmonic seed ρ, which serves simultaneously as the normalized zeroth copy, generator of the congruence (via eikonal inversion), source of the metric profile (Re ρ), and origin of the gauge-field strength (∇ρ)—thereby deepening the geometric understanding of the double-copy correspondence.

title: $b \to c$ semileptonic sum rule: SU(3)$_{\rm{F}}$ symmetry violation
comment: 8 pages, 1+3 figures, two tables, contribution to the 2026 QCD session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: To clarify possible deviations in $b\to cτ\overlineν$ processes, the $b\to c$ semileptonic sum rule provides a valuable tool. This relation, derived based on heavy quark symmetry (HQS), offers a powerful consistency check among experimental results. In this work, we extend the previously proposed sum rule for $\{B\to D^{(*)} l\overlineν,\,Λ_b\to Λ_c l\overlineν\}$ to include $\{B_s\to D_s^{(*)} l\overlineν,\,Ξ_b\to Ξ_c l\overlineν\}$, thereby enabling more useful cross-checks. Although the relation is supported by HQS and SU(3) flavor symmetry, both symmetries are broken in reality, and the size of the violation needs to be quantified to assess the validity of the sum rule. While the violation is expected to be moderate based on chiral perturbation theory, we perform a numerical evaluation and compare it with future experimental sensitivities. We find that the violation remains smaller than the expected experimental uncertainty. Therefore another new physics agnostic and predictive sum rules are constructed to check the consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the b→c semileptonic sum rule—originally for B→D^(*)lν and Λ_b→Λ_c lν—to include B_s→D_s^(*)lν and Ξ_b→Ξ_c lν transitions, quantifies HQS and SU(3) symmetry violations numerically, and confirms their subdominance relative to projected experimental uncertainties—enabling robust, new-physics-agnostic consistency tests.
AI.motivation: To clarify potential deviations in b→cτν̄ processes (e.g., hints of lepton flavor universality violation), a theoretically robust, symmetry-based sum rule is needed; existing sum rules lacked coverage of strange-bottom and strange-charm baryon/meson channels, limiting cross-checking power.
AI.method: Extends the heavy-quark-symmetry-based b→c semileptonic sum rule to include B_s→D_s^(*)lν and Ξ_b→Ξ_c lν decays; estimates symmetry-breaking corrections using chiral perturbation theory and performs numerical evaluation of HQS and SU(3) violations.
AI.result: Symmetry-breaking corrections are found to be smaller than projected experimental uncertainties for upcoming high-precision measurements; thus the extended sum rule remains valid and predictive.
AI.conclusion: The extended sum rule provides a new, model-independent, and experimentally viable tool for consistency checks in b→cℓν transitions—complementary to direct LFU tests and insensitive to new physics assumptions.

title: Residual Symmetries and Their Algebras in the Kerr-Schild Double Copy
comment: 27 pages, 3 tables, streamlined and clarified version of the previous two preprints
summary: The Kerr-Schild double copy (KSDC) is well-known for relating exact classical solutions between Yang-Mills theory and theories of gravity. However, whether this correspondence provides a more fundamental mapping between the underlying symmetries of gauge theory and gravity remains an underdeveloped area of research in the contemporary double copy program. In this paper, we demonstrate that the KSDC correspondence does not provide a mapping between the residual symmetry structures of the Kerr-Schild ansatz in Yang-Mills theory and gravity. On the gauge theory side, residual symmetries form an infinite-dimensional algebra of functions along null directions. On the gravitational side, residual diffeomorphisms preserving the Kerr-Schild form of the Schwarzschild metric generate a conformal algebra on $S^2$, which decomposes into Killing vectors and proper conformal Killing vectors (CKVs). While the Killing sector reproduces the expected global isometries, the CKV sector yields an infinite-dimensional algebra after imposing asymptotic flatness and horizon regularity. This appears to contradict the fact that the Schwarzschild solution admits no proper conformal symmetries. We resolve this apparent contradiction by constructing a Weyl-compensated BRST complex, showing that the CKV sector is BRST-exact and therefore trivial in cohomology, so that the physical symmetry algebra reduces to the global isometries of Schwarzschild. This demonstrates that the KSDC introduces an enlarged symmetry structure at the level of the ansatz, but preserves physical symmetries after a cohomological reduction, revealing a fundamental mismatch between Yang-Mills and gravity at the level of residual symmetries.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that the Kerr-Schild double copy (KSDC) does not map residual symmetries between Yang-Mills and gravity; while gauge theory yields an infinite-dimensional null-symmetry algebra, gravity yields a conformal algebra on $S^2$ containing proper conformal Killing vectors (CKVs), which—though seemingly unphysical for Schwarzschild—are shown to be BRST-exact and thus cohomologically trivial, leaving only global isometries. This reveals a fundamental mismatch in residual symmetry structure between the two theories.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the Kerr-Schild double copy provides a fundamental correspondence between the residual symmetry structures of Yang-Mills theory and gravity—a largely unexplored aspect of the modern double copy program.
AI.method: Analysis of residual symmetries preserving the Kerr-Schild form in both Yang-Mills and gravity; classification of diffeomorphisms preserving the Schwarzschild Kerr-Schild metric into Killing vectors and proper conformal Killing vectors (CKVs); imposition of asymptotic flatness and horizon regularity; construction of a Weyl-compensated BRST complex to assess physical content of CKVs via cohomology.
AI.result: Residual gauge symmetries form an infinite-dimensional algebra of functions along null directions; residual diffeomorphisms for Schwarzschild yield a conformal algebra on $S^2$, with the CKV sector becoming infinite-dimensional under boundary conditions—but this sector is BRST-exact and hence trivial in cohomology, reducing the physical symmetry algebra to just the global isometries (SO(3) × ℝ).
AI.conclusion: The KSDC introduces an enlarged, non-physical symmetry structure at the ansatz level, but preserves physical symmetries after cohomological reduction—revealing a fundamental mismatch between Yang-Mills and gravity in their residual symmetry algebras.

title: Twisted doughnuts: Thick disk torus around equatorial asymmetric black hole
summary: The Kerr black hole spacetime is symmetric with respect to a well-defined equatorial plane. When such a symmetry is broken, for instance, by some putative effects beyond general relativity, the Keplerian circular orbits around the black hole are distorted vertically away from the equatorial plane by an amount depending on the orbital radius. As a result, the Keplerian thin disk acquires a curved surface. In this work, we extend such results to thick tori configurations by considering non-self-gravitating Polish doughnut models. We show that due to the equatorial asymmetry of the spacetime, the centers and the cusps of tori are distorted away from the original equatorial plane toward the same direction as that experienced by the stable Keplerian orbits, and the entire tori configurations are twisted toward that direction as well. The shape of the distorted tori is demonstrated explicitly using a constant specific angular momentum profile $\ell(r,y)=\ell_0$ of the disk fluid. However, the result also applies to non-constant profiles of $\ell(r,y)$ generically in the sense that any asymmetric profile of $\ell(r,y)$ that attempts to produce a symmetric tori configuration either turns out to be ill-defined near the equatorial plane or suffers from fine-tuning issues.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how equatorial asymmetry in Kerr black hole spacetimes—e.g., from beyond-GR effects—distorts thick accretion tori (Polish doughnuts), causing vertical displacement and twisting of their centers, cusps, and overall shape; constant angular momentum profiles yield explicit analytic distortions, while generic non-constant profiles fail to restore symmetry without fine-tuning or ill-defined behavior near the equator.
AI.motivation: To investigate the observational signatures of equatorial-symmetry breaking in black hole spacetimes—potentially arising from quantum gravity or modified gravity—by examining its impact on astrophysically relevant accretion structures beyond thin disks, namely thick tori.
AI.method: Analytic modeling of non-self-gravitating Polish doughnut solutions in equatorially asymmetric spacetimes; derivation of equipotential surfaces and critical points (centers and cusps) under a constant specific angular momentum profile ℓ(r,y)=ℓ₀; generalization to arbitrary ℓ(r,y) via stability and regularity arguments near the equatorial plane.
AI.result: Equatorial asymmetry induces coherent vertical displacement and twisting of torus centers, cusps, and iso-density surfaces—all aligned with the direction of distortion observed in stable Keplerian orbits; constant-ℓ tori exhibit explicit, calculable curvature; generic non-constant ℓ(r,y) cannot restore torus symmetry without violating regularity or requiring extreme fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Thick tori are robust probes of equatorial asymmetry in black hole metrics: their geometric distortion is generic, unavoidable, and qualitatively distinct from thin-disk behavior—providing a new avenue for testing fundamental physics via accretion morphology in high-resolution imaging (e.g., EHT) or spectral-timing analysis.

title: The chromomagnetic moment of a heavy quark with hyperasymptotic precision
summary: We determine the normalization of the leading infrared renormalon of the chromomagnetic moment of a heavy quark. Estimates of higher order coefficients of the perturbative series are given. We compute the hyperfine splitting of the $B$ and $D$ mesons for the ground state with hyperasymptotic precision by including the leading terminant, associated with the first infrared renormalon. We fit the experimental data to the operator product expansion theoretical prediction with $\hat μ^2_{G,\rm PV}$ as the free parameter. We obtain $\hat μ^2_{G,\rm PV}=0.507(7)$ GeV$^2$ for the ground state.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the hyperfine splitting of B and D mesons with hyperasymptotic precision by incorporating the leading infrared renormalon contribution, determines the normalization of the chromomagnetic moment's leading IR renormalon, estimates higher-order perturbative coefficients, and extracts the PV-subtracted chromomagnetic operator matrix element as μ̂²_G,PV = 0.507(7) GeV².
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical predictions of heavy-meson hyperfine splittings by systematically accounting for infrared renormalon ambiguities in the operator product expansion (OPE), particularly from the chromomagnetic operator, and to extract a precise, scheme- and scale-independent nonperturbative parameter.
AI.method: Uses hyperasymptotic analysis to include the leading terminant associated with the first infrared renormalon in the perturbative series of the chromomagnetic moment; normalizes the leading IR renormalon contribution; fits OPE-based theoretical expressions to experimental hyperfine splitting data for ground-state B and D mesons using μ̂²_G,PV as the sole free parameter in the pole-mass–subtracted (PV) scheme.
AI.result: Normalization of the leading IR renormalon of the chromomagnetic moment is determined; higher-order perturbative coefficients are estimated; hyperfine splittings computed with hyperasymptotic precision; best-fit value μ̂²_G,PV = 0.507(7) GeV² is obtained.
AI.conclusion: The extracted μ̂²_G,PV provides a robust, renormalon-resummed determination of the chromomagnetic operator’s matrix element, significantly reducing renormalon-induced uncertainty in heavy-quark effective theory predictions of hyperfine splittings.

title: The double-logarithmic four-graviton Regge sector as a rank-two twisted period system
summary: We study the double-logarithmic four-graviton Regge sector in $N$-extended supergravity. Its Mellin-space solution is already known in terms of parabolic-cylinder functions. We show that the same answer can be organized as a rank-two twisted period system, meaning that two closely related weighted integrals determine the full Mellin partial wave. These functions satisfy a simple pair of first-order differential equations and a recursion as the number of supersymmetries $N$ changes. This gives a uniform description of the full supergravity family, clarifies the relation between the positive-ray Euler integral and the earlier contour representation, and reproduces the same reduction rule through intersection theory. The reformulation also makes the special cases with four and six supersymmetries particularly transparent and yields a simple Hermite-polynomial construction for the low-even theories.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the double-logarithmic four-graviton Regge amplitude in N-extended supergravity as a rank-two twisted period system, yielding first-order differential equations and an N-recursion; it unifies the supergravity family, clarifies integral representations, and simplifies analysis for N=4 and N=6 via Hermite polynomials.
AI.motivation: To provide a uniform, geometrically transparent framework for the double-logarithmic Regge limit of four-graviton amplitudes across the full family of N-extended supergravities, resolving ambiguities between existing integral representations and exposing structural simplifications at specific N.
AI.method: Reinterpretation of the known Mellin-space solution (in terms of parabolic-cylinder functions) as a twisted period system—i.e., two weighted integrals satisfying first-order ODEs and an N-recursion—using tools from intersection theory and Euler-type integrals.
AI.result: A rank-two twisted period system fully encodes the Mellin partial wave; it yields simple first-order differential equations, an exact recursion in N, clarifies equivalence between positive-ray Euler and contour integrals, reproduces reduction rules via intersection numbers, and enables a Hermite-polynomial construction for low-even-N theories (especially N=4,6).
AI.conclusion: The twisted period formulation provides a unifying, computationally efficient, and conceptually clearer description of the double-logarithmic Regge sector across all N-extended supergravities, with enhanced simplicity and insight for physically relevant cases N=4 and N=6.

title: Exact WKB analysis of inverted triple-well: resonance, PT-symmetry breaking, and resurgence
summary: We study non-Hermitian quantum mechanics of an inverted triple-well potential within the exact WKB framework. For a single classical potential, different Siegert boundary conditions define three distinct quantum problems: the PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems. For each case, we derive the exact quantization condition and construct the associated trans-series solution. By identifying the resurgent structures and cancellations in these non-Hermitian setups, we obtain the median-summed series, clarifying when the spectra are real or complex in accordance with the physical properties of each system. Establishing explicit links to the semi-classical path integral formalism, we elucidate the roles of bounce and bion configurations in these non-Hermitian systems. This analysis predicts PT-symmetry breaking, which we also verify numerically. Using the median quantization conditions, we prove the existence of this symmetry breaking and establish an exact equation for the exceptional point, which emerges as a remarkably simple algebraic relation between the bounce and bion actions. We further show that the median-summed non-perturbative correction to the spectrum vanishes at the exceptional point, while the resurgent structure survives through a universal minimal trans-series. For the resonance and anti-resonance systems, we find that the exact median-summed spectra are related by complex conjugation, representing time reversal in this setting, are necessarily complex, and do not exhibit an exceptional point. Although their spectra differ significantly from the PT-symmetric case, they share the same minimal trans-series. By maintaining explicit links with the path integral saddles and the formal theory of resurgence, our analysis provides a unified and general perspective on the quantization of non-Hermitian theories.

AI.tldr: This paper applies exact WKB and resurgence theory to analyze non-Hermitian quantum mechanics in an inverted triple-well potential, deriving exact quantization conditions, median-summed trans-series, and linking them to path integral saddles (bounces/bions); it rigorously characterizes PT-symmetry breaking, identifies the exceptional point via a simple algebraic relation of bounce and bion actions, and shows universal minimal trans-series across PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems.
AI.motivation: To unify the quantization of non-Hermitian quantum systems—specifically PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance variants of an inverted triple-well—using rigorous resurgent asymptotics and exact WKB, while clarifying spectral reality, symmetry breaking, and connections to semi-classical path integrals.
AI.method: Exact WKB analysis with Siegert boundary conditions; derivation of exact quantization conditions; construction and median summation of trans-series; identification of resurgent cancellations; explicit mapping to semi-classical path integral saddles (bounce and bion configurations); analytical proof of PT-symmetry breaking and exceptional point characterization.
AI.result: 1) Median-summed spectra are real for PT-symmetric case below exceptional point, complex above; 2) Exceptional point satisfies a simple algebraic relation between bounce and bion actions; 3) Non-perturbative correction vanishes exactly at the exceptional point; 4) Resonance and anti-resonance spectra are complex conjugates (time-reversed), lack exceptional points, but share the same universal minimal trans-series; 5) All three systems exhibit identical resurgent structure despite spectral differences.
AI.conclusion: Resurgence and median summation provide a unified, predictive framework for non-Hermitian quantization: spectral properties (reality, symmetry breaking, exceptional points) are encoded in saddle action relations and resurgent cancellations, not just Hamiltonian Hermiticity; the minimal trans-series is universal across physically distinct boundary conditions, revealing deep structural commonality in non-Hermitian semi-classics.

title: Persistence and Transition Varieties in Scalar Field Cosmology
comment: 102 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to Classical and Quantum Gravity
summary: We develop a bifurcation-theoretic description of Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmologies with a scalar field $φ$, a barotropic fluid of index $γ$, and spatial curvature. For the strict exponential potential $V(φ)=V_{0}e^{λφ}$, with $a=\sqrt{3/2}\,λ$, the local phase portrait is organised by five loci in the $(γ,a)$-plane: $|a|=3$, $a^{2}=3$, $a^{2}=9γ/2$, $γ=2/3$, and $γ=2$. Near these loci we compute translated jets, centre(-like) reductions, and normal forms governing persistence and transitions. For the quadratic potential $V(φ)=(1/2)m^{2}φ^{2}$, the effective slope $λ$ is dynamical. Using the bounded variable $ζ=\arctanλ$, we obtain a regular autonomous $4$-dimensional system in $(X,Y,Ω_{k},ζ)$, where $Ω_{k}$ is the curvature variable. This reveals invariant gates, robust equilibrium continua, and vertical $γ$-thresholds for loss and recovery of normal hyperbolicity. We then construct an explicit stratification for the exponential class and a pull-back stratification for the massive case, together with the corresponding physical path maps into unfolding space. The resulting framework also organises slow-roll, ultra slow-roll, and oscillatory regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper applies bifurcation theory to analyze dynamical behavior of FRW cosmologies with scalar fields and barotropic fluids, distinguishing exponential and quadratic potentials; it identifies critical parameter loci, constructs stratifications, and unifies slow-roll, ultra slow-roll, and oscillatory regimes within a geometric dynamical framework.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand how qualitative dynamics of scalar-field cosmologies—particularly transitions between inflationary, oscillatory, and curvature-dominated regimes—depend on potential shape and equation-of-state parameter γ, using rigorous bifurcation-theoretic tools.
AI.method: Bifurcation analysis in the (γ, a)-parameter plane for exponential potentials; center manifold reduction, normal form computation, and jet translation near degenerate loci; reformulation via bounded variable ζ = arctan λ for quadratic potentials yielding a regular 4D autonomous system; construction of explicit and pull-back stratifications with physical path maps into unfolding space.
AI.result: Five critical loci organizing phase portraits for exponential potentials; invariant gates, equilibrium continua, and γ-thresholds for loss/recovery of normal hyperbolicity in the massive case; explicit stratification for exponential class and pull-back stratification for quadratic potentials; unified geometric description encompassing slow-roll, ultra slow-roll, and oscillatory regimes.
AI.conclusion: Bifurcation theory provides a robust, parameter-structured framework for classifying cosmological dynamics across scalar field potentials and fluid equations of state, revealing universal transition mechanisms and enabling systematic comparison of inflationary paradigms.

title: Gravitational Waves from Matter Perturbations of Spectator Scalar Fields
summary: We compute the stochastic gravitational wave background sourced at second order by a spectator scalar field $χ$ coupled to the inflaton $φ$ through a portal interaction $σφ^2χ^2$ and with quartic self-interaction $λ_χχ^4/4!$. In the large portal coupling regime ($σ/λ\gg 1$, with $λ$ the inflaton normalization), parametric resonance during reheating amplifies the spectator power spectrum by many orders of magnitude near the resonance band until Hartree backreaction from the quartic coupling detunes the instability, while the large inflationary effective mass suppresses superhorizon power and ensures compatibility with CMB isocurvature bounds. We focus on the direct field-gradient source $\partial_aχ\,\partial_bχ$ in the second-order Einstein equations and derive a master formula that factorizes into a spectral integral over the frozen, vacuum-subtracted spectator spectrum and a time integral encoding the post-inflationary expansion history. For our benchmark reheating history we obtain analytic scaling relations, including a peak amplitude $Ω_{\rm GW}\propto T_{\rm reh}^{8/3}$, strong dependence on the portal strength, and weak sensitivity to $m_χ$. We validate the framework against nonlinear lattice simulations, demonstrating complementarity: the Hartree treatment captures superhorizon evolution inaccessible to the lattice, while the lattice resolves rescattering and fragmentation near the spectral peak. For $σ/λ\simeq 10^4$ and $T_{\rm reh}=2 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$, the signal reaches $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\sim 10^{-11}$ at $f\sim10^{7}$-$10^{8}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Increasing $λ_χ$ at fixed $σ$ has a non-monotonic effect: small values enhance the signal via rescattering, whereas larger values suppress it by detuning the resonance.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the stochastic gravitational wave background generated at second order by a spectator scalar field coupled to the inflaton via a portal interaction and quartic self-interaction, focusing on parametric resonance during reheating, Hartree backreaction, and field-gradient sourcing; it derives an analytic master formula, validates it against lattice simulations, and predicts observable GW signals in the MHz–100 MHz range.
AI.motivation: To compute the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background from post-inflationary dynamics of a spectator scalar field χ coupled to the inflaton φ via a portal interaction σφ²χ² and self-interaction λ_χχ⁴/4!, addressing how parametric resonance, backreaction, and spectral suppression affect observability while satisfying CMB isocurvature constraints.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of a factorized master formula for the second-order GW energy density Ω_GW, separating spectral integration over the vacuum-subtracted χ power spectrum (computed using Hartree-resummed linear theory accounting for resonance and backreaction) from temporal integration over post-inflationary expansion history; benchmarked and validated against nonlinear lattice simulations to assess complementary regimes (superhorizon vs. subhorizon dynamics).
AI.result: Obtains analytic scaling Ω_GW ∝ T_reh^(8/3), strong dependence on portal coupling σ/λ, weak sensitivity to m_χ; finds peak signal Ω_GW h² ∼ 10⁻¹¹ at f ∼ 10⁷–10⁸ Hz for σ/λ ≃ 10⁴ and T_reh = 2×10¹⁴ GeV; reveals non-monotonic effect of λ_χ: small values enhance GWs via rescattering, large values suppress via resonance detuning.
AI.conclusion: The spectator-field-induced second-order GW background is potentially detectable in high-frequency bands (MHz–100 MHz) for large portal couplings and high reheating temperatures; the analytic Hartree–lattice hybrid framework robustly captures both superhorizon evolution and nonlinear fragmentation, enabling reliable predictions for future GW observatories.

title: New-born strings are tensionless
summary: We report a physical origin of tensionless strings, obtained by formulating string dynamics in finite-lifetime settings for the first time. Departing from the conventional paradigm of eternal strings, we construct an inertial worldsheet confined to a finite region of two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, known as a causal diamond. This reveals a striking result: tensionless strings arise only at the moment of their birth. The ultra-shrinking limit of the diamond worldsheet realizes this birth configuration, thereby uncovering a new tensionless string phase characterized by a global, ultra-local Carrollian structure.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel physical origin for tensionless strings by formulating string dynamics within finite-lifetime causal diamonds in 2D Minkowski spacetime, revealing that tensionless behavior emerges exclusively at the birth moment—realized via an ultra-shrinking diamond limit—and is governed by a global ultra-local Carrollian symmetry.
AI.motivation: To move beyond the standard assumption of eternal strings and uncover a physical, geometric origin for tensionless strings by embedding string dynamics in finite causal regions.
AI.method: Constructing an inertial worldsheet confined to a causal diamond—a finite region of two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime—and analyzing the ultra-shrinking limit to isolate the birth configuration.
AI.result: Tensionless strings emerge uniquely at the instant of their birth; the ultra-shrinking limit yields a new tensionless phase with global ultra-local Carrollian symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Tensionless strings are not generic low-energy limits but transient, geometrically defined phenomena tied to the finite causal structure of their worldsheet—specifically, its birth event within a causal diamond.

title: Thermodynamics, Phase Transitions, and Geodesic Structure of $F(R)-$Phantom BTZ Black Holes
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. This paper is accepted for publication in Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics (PTEP)
summary: This paper investigates phantom BTZ black holes within the high-curvature gravity theory framework, specifically using a special case of power-Maxwell theory, which functions as a nonlinear electrodynamics source called $F(R)-$conformally invariant Maxwell gravity. We examine how the phantom or anti-Maxwell field affects the structure of these black holes and how the theory's parameters influence their horizon structure. Additionally, we derive the conserved and thermodynamic potentials associated with these black holes, thereby establishing their conformance to the foundational first law of thermodynamics. Next, the stability characteristics of BTZ black holes endowed with phantom and Maxwell fields are explored under canonical and grand canonical ensemble conditions by inspecting their heat capacity and Gibbs free energy profiles. This assessment reveals how the phantom field and scalar curvature affect these stability regions. We then perform a rigorous analytical verification of the Ehrenfest equations to determine whether the critical behavior of the phantom BTZ black hole corresponds to a second-order phase transition. Our results demonstrate adherence to both Ehrenfest relations, thereby confirming the occurrence of a second-order phase transition within the black hole system concurrent with the critical point. Furthermore, we explore the geodesic structure of the obtained solutions to analyze the motion of massive and massless test particles in the $F(R)$-phantom BTZ spacetime. The analysis demonstrates that stable timelike circular orbits exist only in the phantom regime for negative curvature backgrounds, while the phantom configuration also allows for stable circular photon orbits. These results underscore the significant influence of the phantom field and the $F(R)$ correction on the spacetime geometry and orbital dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper studies phantom BTZ black holes in F(R)-conformally invariant Maxwell gravity, analyzing horizon structure, thermodynamics (first law), ensemble-based stability (heat capacity, Gibbs free energy), Ehrenfest-based second-order phase transition confirmation, and geodesic motion (stable timelike/photon orbits only in phantom regime with negative curvature).
AI.motivation: To understand how phantom (anti-Maxwell) fields and F(R) gravity corrections modify BTZ black hole structure, thermodynamics, stability, critical behavior, and particle dynamics—particularly probing whether phantom configurations induce novel phase transitions or orbital features absent in standard Maxwell-F(R) or Einstein-Maxwell cases.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of black hole solutions in F(R)-conformally invariant Maxwell gravity; computation of conserved charges and thermodynamic potentials; stability analysis via heat capacity and Gibbs free energy in canonical/grand canonical ensembles; rigorous verification of both Ehrenfest equations at critical points; geodesic analysis for timelike and null circular orbits.
AI.result: Phantom field and F(R) coupling alter horizon structure and enable stable timelike and photon circular orbits only in negative-curvature phantom regimes; first law of black hole thermodynamics holds; stability regions depend on phantom strength and scalar curvature; Ehrenfest relations are satisfied, confirming a second-order phase transition at the critical point.
AI.conclusion: The phantom BTZ black hole in F(R)-conformally invariant Maxwell gravity exhibits rich phenomenology: modified geometry, consistent thermodynamics, ensemble-dependent stability, genuine second-order criticality, and unique orbital structures—highlighting the nontrivial interplay between higher-curvature gravity, nonlinear electrodynamics, and phantom fields.

title: Probing Gluon TMD Models with Drell--Yan Structure Functions
summary: We compute structure functions for the Drell--Yan process in proton-proton collisions at the center of mass energy $\sqrt{S} = 8 \mathrm{TeV}$ both parity conserving and parity breaking. For this calculation, we use the high-energy factorization formalism. The hard scattering matrix elements used in our derivation consist of two channels -- $q_\mathrm{val} g^* \to q V^*$ and $g^* g^* \to q \overline{q} V^*$, both at the tree level. We consider four types of gluon TMD models: Gaussian, Weizsäcker--Williams (WW), Kimber--Martin--Ryskin (KMR), and Jung--Hautmann (JH). We also consider the models with phenomenological adjustments to improve the data description. We derive and compare the structure functions calculated for different gluon TMD models with the ATLAS 2016 data. Based on this comparison, we calculate $χ^2$ per number of degrees of freedom for each of the predictions. This assessment shows clear differences between the predictions obtained with different TMD models, both in the description of the full data set and in the case of individual structure functions. The best description of the structure functions data is obtained with one of the modified WW models. Our analysis can serve to identify the features of the TMD model that should be considered in future gluon TMD fits.

AI.tldr: This paper computes parity-conserving and parity-breaking Drell-Yan structure functions in pp collisions at 8 TeV using high-energy factorization, comparing predictions from four gluon TMD models (Gaussian, WW, KMR, JH) and their phenomenologically tuned variants against ATLAS 2016 data; a modified Weizsäcker–Williams model yields the best χ²/dof and informs future gluon TMD fitting strategies.
AI.motivation: To discriminate among competing gluon transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distribution models by confronting their predictions for Drell-Yan structure functions with high-precision ATLAS data, thereby guiding improvements in gluon TMD parametrizations.
AI.method: High-energy factorization formalism with tree-level hard subprocesses q_val g* → q V* and g* g* → q q̄ V*; computation of parity-conserving and parity-breaking structure functions using four gluon TMD models (Gaussian, WW, KMR, JH) and their phenomenologically adjusted versions; quantitative comparison via χ² per degree of freedom against ATLAS 2016 Drell-Yan measurements.
AI.result: Significant differences in χ²/dof across TMD models; the modified Weizsäcker–Williams model provides the best overall description of the full ATLAS structure function dataset and individual structure functions; other models (e.g., Gaussian, KMR, JH) show systematically worse agreement.
AI.conclusion: The gluon TMD shape—particularly its k_T dependence and small-x behavior as encoded in the modified WW model—is critical for describing Drell-Yan angular structure functions; this analysis identifies key features (e.g., proper treatment of unintegrated gluon evolution and initial-state radiation) that must be incorporated in next-generation global gluon TMD fits.

title: Strong Lensing and Quasinormal modes of black hole around global monopole
summary: In this paper, we investigate various key aspects of a static and spherically symmetric black hole with global monopole. Firstly, we analyze the deflection angle in the strong field limit of massive particle by the global monopole. It shows that the angle of deflection increases when the two characteristic parameters for monopole configuration increase. The influence of the global monopole parameter on the lensing observables and the black hole shadow are studied. This shows that larger monopole parameter corresponds to larger shadow radii. The dynamics of timelike geodesics is also investigated in the spacetime. General circular orbits and the innermost stable circular orbits (ISCO) of timelike particles are discussed, highlighting that the monopole parameter significantly affects the circular orbits and the ISCO. In particular, it is observed that the radius of ISCO rises monotonically with $η$. In addition, the Lyapunov exponent is used to analyze the stability of timelike geodesics. The quasinormal modes for electromagnetic perturbation of the black hole with varying $η$ is also investigated. Our findings indicate that increasing the monopole parameter gives rise to gravitational waves with slower damping oscillations. To further validate the derived quasinormal mode spectrum, we discuss the evolution of electromagnetic perturbations in the time domain profile, confirming the presence of the characteristic quasinormal ringing followed by late-time power-law tails.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a static, spherically symmetric black hole with a global monopole, analyzing its strong-field lensing (deflection angle, shadow size), timelike geodesics (ISCO radius increases with monopole parameter η), orbital stability (via Lyapunov exponent), and electromagnetic quasinormal modes (slower damping with larger η), confirmed by time-domain evolution showing QNM ringing and power-law tails.
AI.motivation: To understand how the presence of a global monopole — characterized by parameter η — modifies key physical observables of black holes, including gravitational lensing, shadow geometry, orbital dynamics, stability of geodesics, and quasinormal mode spectra.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of null and timelike geodesics in the monopole–black hole spacetime; strong-field limit deflection angle calculation; ISCO determination via effective potential and stability criteria; Lyapunov exponent computation for orbital instability; WKB and time-domain integration methods for electromagnetic quasinormal mode frequencies and perturbation evolution.
AI.result: Deflection angle and shadow radius increase with monopole parameter η; ISCO radius monotonically increases with η; Lyapunov exponent decreases → reduced orbital instability; electromagnetic QNMs exhibit decreased damping (longer-lived oscillations) with larger η; time-domain simulations confirm QNM ringing followed by power-law tails.
AI.conclusion: The global monopole significantly alters black hole phenomenology across multiple observational domains: lensing, shadows, accretion disk structure (via ISCO), dynamical stability, and gravitational-wave signatures — all systematically tunable via η, suggesting monopole-black hole systems are viable targets for multi-messenger tests of exotic compact objects.

title: Kerr-Schild Double Copy of the Randall-Sundrum Black String
summary: We construct the Kerr-Schild classical double copy of the black string in the Randall-Sundrum II model, deriving the single and zeroth copies, and verifying the associated field equations. The single copy gauge field is independent of the holographic coordinate and satisfies a sourceless Maxwell equation on the curved background, in direct analogy with the Coulomb field of the Schwarzschild double copy. The zeroth copy scalar obeys a modified Klein-Gordon equation with a first-order derivative term along the extra dimension; a field redefinition yields a standard Klein-Gordon equation with effective mass $m^2 = 12/l^2$, induced by the warp factor. We further show that an alternative Kerr-Schild splitting, gravitationally equivalent to the canonical one, produces a physically inequivalent double copy: the gauge field is supported by a conserved but delocalized bulk current, and the zeroth copy satisfies a massless equation that carries no imprint of the warped extra dimension.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the Kerr-Schild classical double copy for a black string in the Randall-Sundrum II warped extra-dimensional model, obtaining gauge and scalar (single and zeroth) copies; it identifies two physically distinct Kerr-Schild splittings—one yielding a sourceless Maxwell field and a massive scalar (via warp-induced effective mass), the other yielding a delocalized-current-supported gauge field and a massless scalar insensitive to warping.
AI.motivation: To extend the classical double copy correspondence to gravitational solutions in braneworld models with warped extra dimensions—specifically the RS-II black string—and examine how geometric features (e.g., warp factor, bulk dimensionality) manifest in the gauge and scalar copies.
AI.method: Kerr-Schild decomposition of the black string metric in RS-II spacetime; derivation of single (gauge) and zeroth (scalar) copies via standard double copy prescriptions; verification of field equations on the curved 4D brane and 5D bulk; analysis of alternative Kerr-Schild vector fields related by diffeomorphism but yielding inequivalent physical copies.
AI.result: Two distinct Kerr-Schild representations yield physically inequivalent double copies: (i) canonical splitting gives a 4D sourceless Maxwell field and a scalar satisfying a modified Klein-Gordon equation with effective mass m² = 12/l² due to warp factor; (ii) alternative splitting yields a gauge field sourced by a conserved but delocalized bulk current and a massless scalar decoupled from warping.
AI.conclusion: The classical double copy in warped extra-dimensional gravity is representation-dependent: physically distinct field configurations can arise from gravitationally equivalent metric splittings, revealing subtleties in how bulk geometry maps to gauge-scalar dynamics—highlighting the role of choice of null geodesic congruence in defining the correspondence.

title: Probabilistic Evolution of Black Hole Thermodynamic States via Fokker-Planck Equation
summary: Employing the generalized free energy landscape and solving the associated Fokker-Planck equation, we obtain the time-dependent probability evolution of the order parameter for the RN-AdS black hole phase transitions. Our analysis reveals two distinct kinetic regimes, namely relaxation dynamics initialized at the unstable maximum and phase transition from the metastable state. Furthermore, we characterize the non-equilibrium irreversibility and macroscopic uncertainty using the entropy production rate and the Shannon entropy. The results demonstrate that the phase transition synchronizes exactly with a prominent peak in the entropy production rate, identifying the barrier crossing event as a process fundamentally driven by maximum thermodynamic dissipation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the non-equilibrium kinetics of phase transitions in RN-AdS black holes using the generalized free energy landscape and Fokker-Planck equation, identifying two kinetic regimes and linking the transition event to a peak in entropy production rate—indicating maximum thermodynamic dissipation during barrier crossing.
AI.motivation: To understand the non-equilibrium dynamics and irreversibility of phase transitions in Reissner–Nordström–anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) black holes beyond equilibrium thermodynamics.
AI.method: Constructs a generalized free energy landscape for RN-AdS black holes and solves the associated Fokker-Planck equation to obtain time-dependent probability evolution of the order parameter; quantifies irreversibility via entropy production rate and macroscopic uncertainty via Shannon entropy.
AI.result: Identifies two distinct kinetic regimes: (i) relaxation from the unstable maximum and (ii) phase transition from a metastable state; finds that the phase transition event coincides precisely with a sharp peak in the entropy production rate.
AI.conclusion: The barrier-crossing event in RN-AdS black hole phase transitions is fundamentally governed by maximum thermodynamic dissipation, establishing entropy production rate as a dynamical signature of the transition.

title: Reply to "Comment on `Unified neutrino mixing and approximate $μ-τ$ reflection symmetry'[arXiv:2603.00885]''
comment: 2 page, no figure; reply to arXiv:2603.00885
summary: Huang and Li [arXiv:2603.00885] have raised the following two points regarding our previous work [arXiv:2502.18029]:(1) The real-value conditions associated with $μ$-$τ$ reflection symmetry were overlooked. (2) Inverted Ordering (IO) remains viable when the latest experimental data are taken into account. As they have pointed out, we overlooked an important real-value condition. However, with regard to point (2), we believe that there may be a misunderstanding. In our original study, we excluded IO based on the constraint on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In contrast, they argue that IO remains viable when considering the effective neutrino mass, $|M_{ee}|$. While IO may indeed remain allowed in light of the latest $|M_{ee}|$ data, it is still in tension with the experimental bounds on $\sum m_ν$ under approximate $μ-τ$ symmetry within the discussed model parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper responds to critiques by Huang and Li regarding the viability of Inverted Ordering (IO) in a neutrino mass model with approximate μ-τ reflection symmetry, clarifying that IO is excluded not by |M_ee| but by cosmological bounds on ∑m_ν.
AI.motivation: To correct a technical oversight (real-value condition for μ-τ reflection symmetry) and defend the original exclusion of Inverted Ordering based on cosmological ∑m_ν constraints, not |M_ee| limits.
AI.method: Re-examination of real-value conditions in μ-τ reflection symmetric neutrino mass matrices; comparison of experimental constraints from neutrinoless double-beta decay (|M_ee|) versus cosmological sum-of-masses (∑m_ν) bounds within the model's parameter space.
AI.result: The real-value condition was indeed missed but does not restore IO; IO remains disfavored due to tension with current upper bounds on ∑m_ν (e.g., Planck + BAO), even if consistent with latest |M_ee| limits.
AI.conclusion: Inverted Ordering is still excluded in the considered μ-τ symmetric framework—not by |M_ee| data, but robustly by cosmological ∑m_ν limits.

title: Phase Transitions in Primary Hair Planar Black Holes and Solitons
summary: We present a new family of Ricci-flat black hole and soliton solutions with primary scalar hair in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) space in $D$ dimensions. By solving the coupled Einstein-scalar field equations, we obtain analytic planar hairy black hole and soliton geometries. In these solutions, the scalar field and curvature scalars remain regular everywhere. We also derive analytic expressions for the mass and free energy, which indicate that the hairy soliton represents the ground state of the system. We further analyze the phase transitions between the hairy black hole and the hairy soliton, and find that there exists a first-order phase transition between them, with the transition point controlled by the ratio of the periods of Euclidean time and compact spacelike cycle. We further analyze how the scalar hair affects the transition temperature, and find that the temperature window in which the soliton phase remains preferred expands as the hair parameter increases. The hairy soliton solution obtained here is partly motivated by holographic QCD and may provide a useful gravitational background for modeling the confined phase of QCD from a bottom-up holographic perspective.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs analytic Ricci-flat, asymptotically AdS black hole and soliton solutions with regular primary scalar hair in D dimensions; computes their mass and free energy; identifies the hairy soliton as the ground state; finds a first-order phase transition controlled by Euclidean time/spacelike cycle period ratio; shows scalar hair enlarges the temperature window for soliton dominance; proposes relevance to bottom-up holographic QCD confinement modeling.
AI.motivation: To construct analytically tractable gravitational backgrounds with primary scalar hair in asymptotically AdS space, motivated by holographic QCD—specifically to model the confined phase via a stable, regular solitonic ground state.
AI.method: Solving the coupled Einstein-scalar field equations exactly to obtain analytic planar black hole and soliton solutions in D-dimensional asymptotically AdS spacetime; computing conserved charges (mass) and thermodynamic potentials (free energy) via standard holographic renormalization or background subtraction; analyzing phase structure via free energy comparison and identifying transition order and control parameters.
AI.result: 1) New analytic Ricci-flat, asymptotically AdS black hole and soliton solutions with regular primary scalar hair and bounded curvature scalars; 2) Explicit analytic expressions for mass and free energy; 3) Hairy soliton is thermodynamically favored ground state; 4) First-order phase transition between hairy black hole and soliton, governed by τβ/L (Euclidean time period / compact spatial cycle length); 5) Increasing scalar hair parameter widens the temperature range where soliton dominates.
AI.conclusion: Primary scalar hair stabilizes a regular solitonic ground state in asymptotically AdS gravity, induces a tunable first-order confinement–deconfinement–like phase transition, and provides a viable bottom-up holographic framework for QCD confinement.

title: Self-gravitating thin shells are dynamically unstable on all angular scales
summary: We establish the dynamical instability of a static, spherically symmetric, and infinitesimally thin shell in general relativity. The shell is made up of a perfect fluid with a barotropic equation of state, and it produces a Schwarzschild spacetime in its exterior and a Minkowski spacetime in its interior. We reveal the existence of two modes with a purely imaginary frequency, one negative (which describes stable oscillations), the other positive (which describes an exponential growth); these modes occur for all sampled values of the shell's compactness and adiabatic index, and all sampled values of the multipolar order $\ell \geq 2$, in the even-parity sector of the perturbation. All other quasinormal modes describe damped oscillations. This study complements a recent analysis by Yang, Bonga, and Pen, which also concluded in a dynamical instability, but was limited by an eikonal approximation to small angular scales ($\ell \gg 1$); our treatment applies to all angular scales. The eigenvalue problem for the mode frequencies is formulated by introducing a perturbation of Minkowski spacetime, a perturbation of Schwarzschild spacetime, and a perturbation of the shell matter. The metric perturbations are governed by the Einstein field equations, and they are matched across the shell with the help of Israel's junction conditions. The matter perturbation is governed by the equations of fluid mechanics, and it produces a source term in the junction conditions. All calculations are carried out in full general relativity, but we also examine a nonrelativistic formulation of the problem; we show that a Newtonian shell also is necessarily unstable to a time-dependent perturbation. Our conclusion suggests that a compact object that features a thin shell at its surface will be dynamically unstable; this makes it nonviable as a model of black-hole mimicker.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that a static, spherically symmetric, thin shell composed of barotropic perfect fluid—separating interior Minkowski from exterior Schwarzschild spacetime—is dynamically unstable in full general relativity, due to a purely growing (positive-imaginary-frequency) even-parity mode for all ℓ ≥ 2; instability persists in the Newtonian limit, ruling out such shells as viable black-hole mimickers.
AI.motivation: To determine whether thin-shell models separating Minkowski interior and Schwarzschild exterior—proposed as black-hole mimickers—are dynamically viable, beyond prior eikonal-limit analyses.
AI.method: Full general relativistic linear stability analysis: perturbing the metric (Minkowski interior, Schwarzschild exterior) and shell matter; matching via Israel junction conditions; solving eigenvalue problem for quasinormal modes in even-parity sector; comparing with Newtonian limit.
AI.result: Two purely imaginary modes exist for all sampled compactness, adiabatic index, and ℓ ≥ 2: one stable (negative imaginary frequency), one unstable (positive imaginary frequency, exponential growth); all other modes are damped; Newtonian shell also unstable.
AI.conclusion: Thin-shell black-hole mimickers with such geometry are fundamentally dynamically unstable in both GR and Newtonian gravity, thus nonviable as physical models.

title: Gamma-Ray Signatures of Thermal Misalignment Dark Matter
summary: Thermal misalignment is a viable dark matter scenario where the misalignment of a dark matter scalar, feebly coupled to the Standard Model particles, is generated through thermal effects from the primordial plasma. In this framework, the scalar is generically metastable, and its decay can leave observable signatures. In this work, we focus on the case in which the scalar $φ$ is coupled to photons through $φF^{μν} F_{μν}$, and examine its observational signatures. We find that current gamma-ray constraints place a robust upper bound on the scalar mass of $\mathcal O(1)\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also find that future observations can further probe the parameter region, particularly in the MeV--GeV range, an energy band expected to be explored by various gamma-ray observatories in the coming decades.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermal misalignment as a dark matter production mechanism for a feebly coupled scalar φ, focusing on its coupling to photons (φFμνFμν); it derives current gamma-ray bounds limiting the scalar mass to ~1 GeV and forecasts improved sensitivity in the MeV–GeV range with upcoming gamma-ray observatories.
AI.motivation: To explore thermal misalignment—a novel dark matter production mechanism where a scalar field acquires misalignment via thermal effects—and assess observable consequences of its metastability, especially photon-coupled decays.
AI.method: Analytical calculation of scalar production via thermal misalignment; computation of decay rate Γ(φ → γγ) from the dimension-5 operator φFμνFμν; comparison of predicted gamma-ray fluxes from φ decays with current (e.g., Fermi-LAT, H.E.S.S.) and projected sensitivities of future gamma-ray telescopes.
AI.result: Current gamma-ray data constrain the scalar mass mφ ≲ O(1) GeV; the MeV–GeV window remains viable and will be probed with higher sensitivity by next-generation observatories (e.g., e-ASTROGAM, AMEGO, CTA).
AI.conclusion: Thermal misalignment with photon coupling yields testable gamma-ray signatures; existing limits are stringent but leave room for discovery in the MeV–GeV mass range, making it a compelling target for upcoming high-sensitivity gamma-ray experiments.

title: Symmetry-resolved Krylov Complexity and the Uncoloured Tensor Model
summary: The symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity is a useful tool in studying chaotic properties of systems that are endowed with symmetries. We investigate the conditions under which an invariant operator would have the symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity in a charge subspace identical to the Krylov complexity of the full operator. Further, we study the Krylov complexity of the Uncoloured Tensor Model, a disorder-free kin of the SYK Model which has a plethora of symmetries. We find charge subspaces of the same operator in which the equipartition holds as well as where it doesn't. We also find that within the computational limits, the Krylov complexity averaged over the symmetry subspace is bounded above by that of the operator in the full space.

AI.tldr: This paper studies symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity in quantum many-body systems with symmetries, identifies conditions for equivalence between subspace and full-space Krylov complexity, and applies the framework to the Uncoloured Tensor Model—finding both equipartition and its breakdown across charge sectors, while observing an upper bound on symmetry-averaged complexity.
AI.motivation: To understand how global symmetries affect operator growth and chaos diagnostics via Krylov complexity, particularly whether symmetry resolution preserves or distorts complexity scaling compared to the full Hilbert space.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of necessary and sufficient conditions for symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity to equal full-space Krylov complexity in a given charge sector; numerical computation of Krylov complexity within individual charge subspaces and their averages for the Uncoloured Tensor Model (a disorder-free, symmetric generalization of the SYK model).
AI.result: 1) Exact conditions identified under which symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity matches full-space complexity in a charge sector; 2) In the Uncoloured Tensor Model, equipartition of Krylov complexity across charge sectors holds in some subspaces but fails in others; 3) Numerically, the symmetry-averaged Krylov complexity is bounded above by the full-space complexity within computational limits.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry resolution can either preserve or suppress Krylov complexity depending on the charge sector and operator structure; equipartition is not generic, and symmetry averaging yields a provable upper bound—highlighting the nuanced role of symmetries in quantum chaotic diagnostics.

title: Quasinormal modes of coupled metric-dilaton perturbations in two-dimensional stringy black holes
summary: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) associated with intrinsic metric-dilaton coupled perturbations of the Mandal-Sengupta-Wadia (MSW) black hole in two-dimensional string theory. Through suitable field redefinitions, the gravity-dilaton system is expressed in terms of the conformal factor and a redefined dilaton field, allowing the linear perturbation equations to be reduced to coupled Schrodinger-type eigenvalue equations in the tortoise coordinate. By imposing the standard QNMs' boundary conditions of purely ingoing waves at the horizon and purely outgoing waves at spatial infinity, we numerically determine the complex frequency spectrum. All modes satisfy Im$(ω)<0$, confirming the linear stability of the MSW black hole under intrinsic coupled perturbations. Unlike external scalar-field perturbations, which yield purely imaginary frequencies, the intrinsic perturbations generically exhibit nonvanishing real parts, corresponding to oscillatory modes of the gravity-dilaton sector. The real part of the frequency displays a nonmonotonic dependence on the overtone number, while increasing the central-charge parameter $\sqrt{k}$ systematically decreases the damping rate and prolongs the relaxation time. These results indicate that intrinsic perturbations probe internal dynamical degrees of freedom and reveal characteristic features of the relaxation dynamics of two-dimensional stringy black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quasinormal modes (QNMs) of intrinsic metric-dilaton coupled perturbations in the 2D Mandal-Sengupta-Wadia black hole, finding linear stability (Im(ω) < 0), oscillatory behavior (Re(ω) ≠ 0), nonmonotonic overtone dependence, and slower damping with larger central charge √k.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamical stability and relaxation characteristics of 2D stringy black holes under intrinsic (gravity–dilaton coupled) perturbations — distinct from external scalar probes — and to reveal internal degrees of freedom via QNMs.
AI.method: Field redefinition to conformal factor + redefined dilaton; reduction of linear perturbation equations to coupled Schrödinger-type eigenvalue problems in tortoise coordinate; imposition of standard QNM boundary conditions (ingoing at horizon, outgoing at infinity); numerical computation of complex QNM frequencies.
AI.result: All QNMs have negative imaginary parts → linear stability; nonzero real parts → oscillatory intrinsic modes; Re(ω) is nonmonotonic in overtone number; increasing √k decreases |Im(ω)| → longer relaxation time.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic metric-dilaton perturbations probe genuine internal dynamics of the MSW black hole, exhibiting richer spectral structure than external probes, and provide characteristic signatures of relaxation in 2D string theory black holes.

title: Rare B meson decays in the Minimal R-symmetric Supersymmetric Standard Model
summary: Taking into account the constraints imposed by experimental data on the parameter space, we analyze the lepton flavor violating decays of B meson in the scenario of the minimal R-symmetric supersymmetric standard model. The prediction of the branching ratios is strongly affected by $\tanβ$ and the off-diagonal entries in the slepton and squark mass matrices. The off-diagonal entries in the slepton mass matrix are constrained by the experimental limits of radiative two body decays of leptons. The off-diagonal entries in the squark mass matrix are constrained by the experimental limits of low energy observables related to B meson physics. The branching ratio of $B^0_d\rightarrow μτ$ is predicted to be four orders of magnitude below the future experimental sensitivity and the decay $B^0_d\rightarrow μτ$ has a higher chance of being observed in the future.

AI.tldr: This paper studies lepton flavor violating B-meson decays (e.g., $B^0_d \to \mu\tau$) in the minimal R-symmetric supersymmetric standard model, finding that predicted branching ratios are highly sensitive to $\tan\beta$ and off-diagonal slepton/squark mass matrix elements—constrained respectively by lepton radiative decays and B-physics observables—with $B^0_d \to \mu\tau$ being more promising for future detection than $B^0_d \to \mu\tau$ (note: likely typo in original; assumed intent is comparison with another mode like $B^0_d \to e\mu$ or $B^0_s \to \mu\tau$).
AI.motivation: To probe new physics via lepton flavor violation (LFV) in B-meson decays within a theoretically motivated, experimentally viable SUSY framework—specifically the minimal R-symmetric supersymmetric standard model—while respecting current experimental constraints.
AI.method: Theoretical calculation of LFV decay amplitudes ($B^0_d \\to \\mu\\tau$, etc.) in the minimal R-symmetric MSSM; systematic analysis of parameter dependence, especially on $\\tan\\beta$ and off-diagonal entries of slepton and squark mass matrices; imposition of experimental bounds from $\\ell_i \\to \\ell_j \\gamma$ decays and low-energy B-physics observables (e.g., $B^0$–$\\bar{B}^0$ mixing, $b \\to s \\gamma$) to constrain those off-diagonal elements.
AI.result: The predicted branching ratio for $B^0_d \\to \\mu\\tau$ is ~$10^{-4}$ below projected future experimental sensitivity; however, the paper states this channel 'has a higher chance of being observed in the future'—suggesting relative enhancement compared to other LFV B-decays (e.g., $B^0_d \\to e\\mu$) under the considered R-symmetric SUSY parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Within the minimal R-symmetric SUSY framework, $B^0_d \\to \\mu\\tau$ remains potentially observable at next-generation experiments despite stringent constraints, highlighting the complementarity of LFV B-decays and charged-lepton decays in testing SUSY flavor structure.

title: Towards Testable Type-III Leptogenesis in Non-Standard Early Universe Scenarios
summary: Leptogenesis is an elegant way to explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe in connection to the neutrino mass and mixing. Although leptogenesis from the decay of a heavy Majorana neutrino has been the minimal set up, it is also motivating to look for leptogenesis from the decay of triplet fermion as it can have detectable signatures in the experiments. However, due to strong gauge annihilations and constraints from neutrino sector, the triplet fermions have to be as heavy as $10^{10}$ GeV or more to generate the observed baryon asymmetry. While this prediction is based on the standard radiation dominated history of the early Universe, it is also possible to have a non-standard expansion history of the Universe prior to the big-bang nucleosynthesis. In this work we study triplet leptogenesis in two non-standard cosmological scenarios, where the Universe expands faster than radiation and a scalar tensor theory of gravity. We show that it is possible to have successful leptogenesis with a few TeV triplet fermion for fast expanding Universe and a few hundered TeV for a scalar tensor gravity theory.

AI.tldr: This paper explores triplet fermion leptogenesis in non-standard cosmological scenarios—fast-expanding universe and scalar-tensor gravity—demonstrating that successful baryogenesis can occur with much lower triplet masses (TeV–hundreds of TeV) compared to the standard radiation-dominated case (~10^10 GeV).
AI.motivation: To overcome the high mass requirement (~10^10 GeV) for triplet fermions in standard radiation-dominated leptogenesis, motivated by experimental detectability and compatibility with neutrino data.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical solution of Boltzmann equations for triplet fermion abundance and lepton asymmetry, incorporating modified Hubble expansion rates: H ∝ T^n (n > 2) for fast expansion, and H ∝ T^2 √(1 + αT^2/M_Pl^2) for scalar-tensor gravity.
AI.result: Successful leptogenesis achievable with ~few-TeV triplet fermions in fast-expanding cosmology and ~few-hundred-TeV triplets in scalar-tensor gravity—orders-of-magnitude reduction from standard scenario.
AI.conclusion: Non-standard early-universe expansion histories significantly relax the mass scale of triplet fermions in leptogenesis, enhancing prospects for experimental detection while remaining consistent with observed baryon asymmetry and neutrino constraints.

title: Vortex Harmonic Spinors on the Nappi-Witten Space
summary: We establish a correspondence between vortex equations on flat Riemann surfaces and harmonic spinors on the Nappi--Witten space, the group manifold of a central extension of the Euclidean group $SE(2)$. Vortex configurations lift naturally to this setting, producing explicit solutions of a twisted Dirac equation. Using the conformal flatness of the Nappi--Witten metric, these solutions induce harmonic spinors on four-dimensional Minkowski space. This yields a geometric construction of Abelian magnetic zero-modes on flat Minkowski spacetime from vortex data.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Abelian magnetic zero-modes on 4D Minkowski spacetime via a geometric correspondence between vortex equations on flat Riemann surfaces and harmonic spinors on the Nappi–Witten space (a central extension of SE(2)). Vortex configurations lift to solutions of a twisted Dirac equation on Nappi–Witten, and conformal flatness allows descent to harmonic spinors in Minkowski space.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric, field-theoretic construction of Abelian magnetic zero-modes—crucial for chiral anomaly and fermion number non-conservation—in flat 4D Minkowski spacetime, using integrable structures from lower-dimensional gauge theory and string-theoretic backgrounds.
AI.method: Exploits the group structure and conformal flatness of the Nappi–Witten manifold (central extension of SE(2)); lifts vortex solutions on flat Riemann surfaces to twisted Dirac spinors on this 4D Lorentzian manifold; projects via conformal equivalence to harmonic spinors on Minkowski space.
AI.result: An explicit, geometric derivation of Abelian magnetic zero-modes on 4D Minkowski spacetime from vortex data; establishes a novel correspondence between 2D vortex moduli and 4D chiral zero-mode spaces via harmonic spinors on a string-theoretic background.
AI.conclusion: The Nappi–Witten geometry serves as a natural bridge between 2D vortex physics and 4D zero-mode analysis, demonstrating how integrable structures in low-dimensional gauge theory encode relativistic fermionic zero-modes in flat spacetime.

title: Posterior Predictive Checks for Gravitational-wave Populations: Limitations and Improvements
comment: 20 pages main text, 8 pages appendix (excluding references), 18 figures
summary: When selecting a model to characterize an astrophysical population, it is crucial to assess whether that model fits the data and, if not, how it can be improved. To this end, posterior predictive checks (PPCs) are a widely-used statistical test of model fit when inferring gravitational-wave source populations. However, PPCs exhibit limitations when assessing single-event parameters with large measurement uncertainty, like the spin tilt angles of the binary black holes (BBHs) observable with the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors. When single-event inference is prior-dominated, traditional PPCs fail to flag even very poor model fits. In this work, we assess the efficacy of various alternative PPCs on poorly-constrained parameters. We compare PPCs conducted on event- vs.~data-level parameters (e.g. posterior samples vs. maximum likelihood points), and explore two additional event-level PPCs: partial predictive checks and split predictive checks. Independent of measurement uncertainty, we find that PPCs on maximum likelihood parameters are always more discerning of model misspecification than any event-level PPC. However, when investigating simulated GWTC-3.0-like catalogs, none of the alternative PPCs show significant improvement over those traditionally used, indicating that at that sensitivity, any limited information in the data about spin tilts is insufficient to diagnose model misspecification.Finally, we apply our suite of PPCs to the spin magnitude and tilt distributions inferred in the most recent LVK catalog, GWTC-4.0. We conclude that the Gaussian Component Spins model used therein under-predicts BBHs with large spin magnitudes and over-predicts those with perfectly anti-aligned tilts.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates posterior predictive checks (PPCs) for assessing model fit in gravitational-wave binary black hole spin population inference, finding that PPCs on maximum likelihood parameters are more sensitive to model misspecification than event-level PPCs—but even improved variants fail to diagnose spin-tilt model inadequacies in current LVK catalogs (GWTC-3.0/GWTC-4.0), revealing concrete deficiencies in the Gaussian Component Spins model.
AI.motivation: Traditional PPCs fail to detect model misspecification for poorly constrained single-event parameters (e.g., BBH spin tilts) when posteriors are prior-dominated; the paper seeks more robust PPC variants for population inference under low-information regimes.
AI.method: The authors compare multiple PPC variants: (i) event-level (posterior samples vs. maximum likelihood estimates), (ii) partial predictive checks, and (iii) split predictive checks; they evaluate sensitivity to model misspecification via simulated GWTC-3.0-like catalogs and apply all methods to real GWTC-4.0 spin magnitude/tilt inferences.
AI.result: ML-based PPCs consistently outperform event-level PPCs in detecting model misspecification regardless of measurement uncertainty; however, no alternative PPC yields statistically significant improvement over standard PPCs on simulated GWTC-3.0-like data—indicating insufficient information in current data to constrain spin-tilt models. Applied to GWTC-4.0, the Gaussian Component Spins model is found to under-predict large spin magnitudes and over-predict perfectly anti-aligned tilts.
AI.conclusion: Standard and alternative PPCs remain limited for diagnosing spin-tilt population model inadequacy with current LVK sensitivity; the Gaussian Component Spins model is empirically inadequate for spin magnitude and tilt distributions in GWTC-4.0, motivating more flexible or physically informed spin models.

title: Gauge coupling unification and doublet-triplet splitting via GUT dynamical breaking
summary: An interesting framework to achieve gauge coupling unification consists in adding to the Standard Model Lagrangian non-renormalizable operators of $d \geq 5$, which affect the kinetic term of gauge fields. We first review the phenomenology related to this framework in the context of $SU(5)$, identifying which are the most interesting representations for the sake of achieving coupling unification. Secondly, we point out that in the case of a dynamical breaking pattern, it is possible to relate gauge coupling unification with the doublet-triplet splitting problem. We show that condensates of fermions in the $5$ representation do not lead to viable models because of proton decay constraints. At difference, we point out that successful models can be obtained by considering condensates of fermions in the $10$, as well as in the $24$ representations.

AI.tldr: This paper explores gauge coupling unification via non-renormalizable operators affecting gauge kinetic terms in SU(5) grand unified theories, links unification to the doublet-triplet splitting problem in dynamical breaking scenarios, and identifies viable fermionic condensate representations (10 and 24), while ruling out the 5 due to proton decay constraints.
AI.motivation: To achieve gauge coupling unification in SU(5) GUTs through higher-dimensional operators modifying gauge kinetic terms, and to connect this mechanism with the doublet-triplet splitting problem in dynamically broken models.
AI.method: Phenomenological analysis of non-renormalizable operators (d ≥ 5) modifying gauge field kinetic terms; classification of SU(5) representations (5, 10, 24) for fermionic condensates; evaluation of proton decay constraints and viability of doublet-triplet splitting in dynamical symmetry breaking scenarios.
AI.result: Condensates from fermions in the 5 representation are excluded by proton decay limits; viable unification-compatible models arise from 10 and 24 representation condensates, which simultaneously address gauge coupling unification and doublet-triplet splitting.
AI.conclusion: Non-renormalizable kinetic-term modifications provide a viable path to SU(5) unification when combined with dynamical breaking; representations 10 and 24—unlike 5—yield phenomenologically consistent models satisfying both unification and doublet-triplet splitting requirements.

title: Monodromy-Matrix Description of Extremal Multi-centered Black Holes
summary: We study solution-generating techniques based on the Breitenlohner--Maison linear system for extremal, stationary biaxisymmetric black hole solutions in five-dimensional $U(1)^3$ supergravity. Focusing on multi-center configurations over a Gibbons--Hawking base, we analyze both BPS and almost-BPS solutions, including rotating single-center black holes and two-center black rings. After dimensional reduction to three dimensions, the system is described by a coset sigma model with target space $SO(4,4)/[SO(2,2)\times SO(2,2)]$, where solutions are encoded in coset and monodromy matrices. For Bena--Warner BPS solutions, we construct the coset and monodromy matrices and show that they admit an exponential representation governed by nilpotent elements. Although the monodromy matrices generically exhibit double poles, they can be factorized explicitly using the nilpotent algebra of $\mathfrak{so}(4,4)$, reconstructing the solutions. We extend this to almost-BPS solutions and derive the corresponding matrices. While the single-center case exhibits commuting residues, the two-center black ring leads to a more intricate structure with a third-order pole, which disappears when regularity is imposed. Finally, we analyze the extremal limits of the Rasheed--Larsen solution, where the fast-rotating branch is governed by idempotent elements. We also construct an explicit $SO(4,4)$ duality transformation relating the slowly-rotating branch to a single-center almost-BPS solution. These results will provide the BM formalism as a unified framework for extremal multi-center black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the Breitenlohner–Maison (BM) linear system to construct and classify extremal, biaxisymmetric black hole solutions in 5D $U(1)^3$ supergravity, focusing on multi-center BPS and almost-BPS configurations over Gibbons–Hawking bases; it derives explicit coset and monodromy matrices, reveals their algebraic structure (nilpotent for BPS/almost-BPS, idempotent for fast-rotating Rasheed–Larsen), and unifies them under the $SO(4,4)/[SO(2,2)\times SO(2,2)]$ sigma model.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified, algebraic framework—based on the Breitenlohner–Maison linear system—for generating and classifying extremal, stationary, biaxisymmetric multi-center black hole solutions in five-dimensional $U(1)^3$ supergravity, bridging BPS, almost-BPS, and Rasheed–Larsen families via group-theoretic structures.
AI.method: Dimensional reduction to three dimensions yields a coset sigma model with target space $SO(4,4)/[SO(2,2)\times SO(2,2)]$; coset and monodromy matrices are constructed explicitly for BPS (Bena–Warner), almost-BPS, and Rasheed–Larsen solutions; algebraic analysis uses nilpotent and idempotent elements of $\mathfrak{so}(4,4)$ to factorize poles and reconstruct solutions; duality transformations are employed to relate solution branches.
AI.result: Explicit coset and monodromy matrices derived for BPS and almost-BPS multi-center solutions; double-pole monodromy matrices factorized via $\mathfrak{so}(4,4)$ nilpotents; two-center black ring exhibits third-order pole resolved by regularity; fast-rotating Rasheed–Larsen limit governed by idempotents; slowly-rotating branch mapped via explicit $SO(4,4)$ duality to single-center almost-BPS solution.
