AI.conclusion: The Breitenlohner–Maison formalism provides a unified, algebraically transparent framework for extremal multi-center black holes in 5D $U(1)^3$ supergravity, where solution classification and generation reduce to the representation theory of $\mathfrak{so}(4,4)$—specifically, nilpotent (BPS/almost-BPS) and idempotent (certain extremal non-BPS) elements—thereby generalizing and connecting previously disparate solution families.

title: Algebraic approach to quantum gravity IV: applications
summary: We provide a relatively self-contained introduction to the application of quantum spacetime and quantum Riemannian geometry to theoretical physics. Recent successes include calculation of the vacuum energy of spacetime curvature fluctuations in a single-plaquette model of quantum gravity, derivation of the Kaluza-Klein ansatz as a consequence of quantum spacetime, exactly conserved Noether charges from variational calculus on a lattice, and a new theory of classical and quantum geodesics. The latter leads to a theory of generally covariant quantum mechanics applicable in General Relativity with intriguing first results for the case of a black-hole. We discuss several open problems past and present, and how they might be addressed going forward. New results include a phase transition for Euclidean quantum gravity on a 4-pointed star.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces quantum spacetime and quantum Riemannian geometry to theoretical physics, reporting advances including vacuum energy calculations in a single-plaquette quantum gravity model, derivation of the Kaluza-Klein ansatz from quantum spacetime, lattice-based exactly conserved Noether charges, and a new generally covariant quantum mechanics framework with applications to black holes; it also reports a phase transition in Euclidean quantum gravity on a 4-pointed star.
AI.motivation: To provide a self-contained introduction to quantum spacetime and quantum Riemannian geometry and demonstrate their applicability to foundational problems in theoretical physics—including quantum gravity, unification, symmetry conservation, and quantum mechanics in curved spacetime.
AI.method: Application of quantum spacetime formalism and quantum Riemannian geometry; variational calculus on discrete lattices; construction of quantum geodesic equations; analysis of Euclidean quantum gravity on finite topologies (e.g., 4-pointed star).
AI.result: Vacuum energy of curvature fluctuations computed in a single-plaquette model; Kaluza-Klein metric ansatz derived as emergent from quantum spacetime structure; exact lattice Noether charges obtained; a new theory of quantum geodesics formulated, enabling generally covariant quantum mechanics with black-hole applications; discovery of a phase transition in Euclidean quantum gravity on a 4-pointed star.
AI.conclusion: Quantum spacetime and quantum Riemannian geometry offer a coherent, computationally tractable framework for addressing long-standing issues in quantum gravity and quantum field theory in curved spacetime; the results support further development of discrete, background-independent approaches with testable phenomenological consequences.

title: Cosmological collider signals of modular spontaneous CP breaking
summary: We consider a modular-invariant extension of the Standard Model. Assuming that the modulus is the inflaton, the CP-violating phases of the Yukawa couplings evolve during inflation. This dynamics favours a Higgs condensate, so that Standard Model fermions mediate a one-loop cosmological collider signal enhanced by chemical potentials. Next-generation experiments can probe sub-Planckian values of the modulus decay constant. We provide precise expressions for Dirac fermions with chemical potentials in de Sitter.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modular-invariant extension of the Standard Model where the modulus field acts as the inflaton; CP-violating Yukawa phases evolve during inflation, enhancing a one-loop cosmological collider signal via fermion-mediated Higgs condensation, with detectable signatures for next-generation experiments probing sub-Planckian modulus decay constants.
AI.motivation: To explore testable cosmological signatures of modular invariance in beyond-Standard-Model physics, particularly linking inflation dynamics, CP violation, and quantum effects in de Sitter space.
AI.method: Analyzes evolution of CP-violating Yukawa phases during inflation in a modular-invariant SM extension; computes one-loop cosmological collider signals mediated by Dirac fermions with chemical potentials in de Sitter spacetime; derives precise analytical expressions for such contributions.
AI.result: Demonstrates that Higgs condensation is dynamically favoured; obtains enhanced cosmological collider signals due to chemical-potential–driven fermionic loops; shows next-generation experiments can probe modulus decay constants below the Planck scale.
AI.conclusion: Modular-invariant inflationary scenarios generate observable, loop-level cosmological collider signals—enabled by time-varying CP phases and fermionic chemical potentials in de Sitter—providing a novel pathway to constrain quantum gravity-motivated symmetries.

title: Probing the Factorized Island Branch with the Capacity of Entanglement in JT Gravity
summary: Black hole islands are usually diagnosed through the von Neumann entropy, but the full replica saddle contains more information than survives in the limit $n \to 1$. In this paper we show that the capacity of entanglement can detect that extra structure already within the controlled factorized island branch of JT gravity coupled to a large-$c$ bath. In the late-time high-temperature regime, the entropy plateau remains unchanged at the first nontrivial order, while the capacity acquires a definite correction. This provides a sharp semiclassical example in which nearby replica data are physically meaningful even when the entropy itself appears rigid. Our result shows that the factorized island saddle already carries finite-$n$ information beyond the entropy, and that the capacity is a natural observable for exposing it. More broadly, it highlights that the physics of island saddles is not exhausted by the $n=1$ limit: the surrounding replica geometry can contain additional, and observable, information about how the semiclassical saddle is assembled.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the capacity of entanglement—beyond von Neumann entropy—reveals finite-n replica structure in JT gravity with a large-c bath, showing that island saddles encode physically meaningful information beyond the n→1 limit.
AI.motivation: To probe whether replica geometry beyond the n → 1 limit (i.e., finite-n corrections) carries physical information about island saddles, since von Neumann entropy alone is insensitive to such structure in the factorized island branch.
AI.method: Analytical computation of the capacity of entanglement (second derivative of Rényi entropy at n = 1) within the controlled factorized island saddle in Jackiw–Teitelboim (JT) gravity coupled to a large-c conformal bath, focusing on the late-time, high-temperature regime.
AI.result: The von Neumann entropy plateau remains uncorrected at leading nontrivial order, while the capacity of entanglement acquires a definite, nonzero correction—proving finite-n structure is physically detectable even in the semiclassically controlled factorized saddle.
AI.conclusion: The capacity of entanglement serves as a sharp semiclassical probe of finite-n replica data encoded in island geometries; thus, island physics extends meaningfully beyond the n = 1 entropy limit and involves observable geometric structure in the replica manifold.

title: A Survey through Conformal Time
summary: We revisit conformal time $η$ in a spatially flat Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe and use a $1+1$-dimensional setting as a technically transparent pedagogical arena. Our purpose is to clarify the relation among cosmic time $t$, conformal time $η$, and the scale factor $a(t)$, and then to follow how this relation governs the geodesics of freely moving particles and the curvature of the corresponding manifold. The radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and exact vacuum-only de Sitter cases are treated separately, because each of them produces a distinct conformal-time dependence and therefore a distinct geodesic structure. We then write the affine-parameter formalism in a form that is genuinely general for any spatially flat conformal metric, and we record the straightforward extension to the spatially flat $3+1$ case. The presentation remains elementary in spirit, but the notation, the curvature formulas, and the de Sitter interpretation are kept explicit.

AI.tldr: This paper clarifies the roles and interrelations of cosmic time t, conformal time η, and scale factor a(t) in spatially flat FRW cosmologies using a simplified 1+1D framework; it analyzes geodesics and curvature for radiation-, matter-, and vacuum-dominated (de Sitter) cases, and generalizes the affine-parameter formalism to any spatially flat conformal metric.
AI.motivation: To clarify the conceptual and mathematical relationship among cosmic time t, conformal time η, and scale factor a(t), and to understand how this relationship determines particle geodesics and spacetime curvature in spatially flat cosmological models.
AI.method: Uses a pedagogically transparent 1+1-dimensional Friedmann–Robertson–Walker (FRW) setting with spatial flatness; analytically treats radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and exact de Sitter universes separately; derives and interprets geodesics via affine parameter formalism; computes curvature explicitly; extends results to 3+1 dimensions.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for η(t) and a(η) in each cosmological era; distinct geodesic behaviors and causal structures tied to conformal-time parametrization; general affine-parameter equations valid for any spatially flat conformally flat metric; curvature scalars (e.g., Ricci scalar) expressed in terms of a(η); clear geometric interpretation of de Sitter spacetime in conformal coordinates.
AI.conclusion: Conformal time η is not merely a coordinate choice but fundamentally shapes geodesic structure and curvature interpretation; the functional form of a(η) dictates causal and kinematic properties of freely falling particles; the affine-parameter formalism unifies treatment across all spatially flat conformal cosmologies.

title: Absorption and quasinormal modes by rotating acoustic black holes in Lorentz-violating background
summary: In this work, we investigate the effects of Lorentz symmetry violation on the absorption cross section and quasinormal modes of a rotating acoustic black hole in (2+1) dimensions. The absorption cross section was analyzed analytically, using the low and high frequency regimes, and numerically, through integration of the radial equation. The results showed that Lorentz violation increases the absorption cross section at all energy scales, with a contribution from the rotation parameter $B$ appearing even in the low frequency regime. For the quasinormal modes, we observed that symmetry breaking decreases the real part of the frequencies and increases the magnitude of the corresponding imaginary part, indicating a faster damping of the oscillations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how Lorentz symmetry violation affects absorption cross sections and quasinormal modes of a (2+1)-dimensional rotating acoustic black hole, finding enhanced absorption and faster damping of oscillations.
AI.motivation: To explore physical consequences of Lorentz symmetry violation in analogue gravity systems, specifically its impact on scattering and stability properties of rotating acoustic black holes.
AI.method: Analytical treatment of absorption cross section in low- and high-frequency limits; numerical integration of the radial wave equation; analysis of quasinormal mode frequencies via boundary conditions for purely ingoing waves at the horizon and outgoing waves at infinity.
AI.result: Lorentz violation enhances the absorption cross section across all energies, with rotational coupling appearing even at low frequencies; it reduces the real part and increases the magnitude of the imaginary part of quasinormal frequencies, implying shorter-lived oscillations.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz symmetry breaking significantly modifies both the scattering and dynamical response of rotating acoustic black holes, serving as a potential observational signature in analogue systems.

title: Pion Parton Distribution Functions in the Light-Cone Quark Model and Experimental Constraints
summary: In this work, we investigate the valence quark parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the pion within the light-cone quark model. The initial quark PDFs are calculated by solving the quark-quark correlation function for the pseudoscalar mesons. The initial quark PDFs have been evolved to higher energy scales through the Dokshitzer,Gribov,Lipatov,Altarelli,Parisi (DGLAP) evolution equations. We also find that our calculated evolved PDFs match experimental and available theoretical extraction data. For the first time, we have also predicted the $F_2$ structure function at next-to-leading (NLO) order accuracy. The calculated $F_2$ structure function has been compared with the available ZEUS and H1 experimental data at DESY-HERA over a wide range of energy scales. Additionally, we display the forward pion production cross-section for the Drell-Yan process caused by pions using the pion PDFs that were calculated and the target nucleon PDFs from the LHAPDF nucleus datasets. The evolved $F_2$ structure function of the pion have been studied at the upcoming electron-ion collider energy kinematics. Overall, it was observed that the quark PDFs of pions computed using the light-cone quark model consistent with the experimental results.

AI.tldr: This paper computes pion valence quark PDFs using the light-cone quark model, evolves them via DGLAP equations, validates against experimental and theoretical data, predicts the pion $F_2$ structure function at NLO, compares it with ZEUS/H1 data, computes Drell-Yan cross sections, and projects results to EIC kinematics—all showing consistency with experiment.
AI.motivation: To provide a theoretically robust and phenomenologically viable determination of pion valence quark PDFs and related observables (e.g., $F_2$, Drell-Yan cross sections) that are poorly constrained experimentally but essential for QCD studies and future EIC physics.
AI.method: Light-cone quark model calculation of initial pion quark-quark correlation function → derivation of initial valence quark PDFs → NLO DGLAP evolution to higher scales → computation of NLO $F_2$ structure function → convolution with nucleon PDFs (LHAPDF) for Drell-Yan cross sections → comparison with ZEUS/H1 data and EIC kinematic projections.
AI.result: Evolved pion valence PDFs agree with experimental and theoretical extractions; NLO $F_2$ matches ZEUS/H1 data across HERA $Q^2$ and $x$ ranges; Drell-Yan forward pion production cross sections are quantitatively predicted; $F_2$ is projected to be measurable at EIC.
AI.conclusion: The light-cone quark model yields pion valence PDFs consistent with current data and enables reliable predictions for key hadronic structure observables, supporting its use in QCD phenomenology and future collider analyses.

title: Edge modes in Chern-Simons theory on a strip
comment: 18 pages, no figures, accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: We investigate abelian Chern-Simons gauge theory on a strip geometry with two spatial boundaries. In the presence of boundaries, gauge invariance is broken by boundary conditions, leading to physical edge excitations. By deriving the most general local boundary conditions consistent with power counting in the sense of Symanzik, we show that the bulk equations of motion determine the boundary degrees of freedom through a broken gauge Ward identity, yielding boundary Kac-Moody current algebras with opposite central charges on the two edges. The corresponding two-dimensional boundary actions are of Tomonaga-Luttinger type and describe chiral bosons propagating in opposite directions along the two boundaries. A consistency condition, interpreted as a holographic-like bulk-boundary matching, relates the Chern-Simons coupling constant and the boundary parameters to the physical edge velocities. Within this framework, the equality and opposite sign of the two velocities in a symmetric setup follow directly from the boundary structure rather than from model-dependent assumptions about confining potentials, and the velocities are independent of the strip width. Our analysis provides a fully field-theoretic realization of bulk-boundary correspondence in Chern-Simons theory with two boundaries, with direct applications to edge physics in quantum Hall systems and related topological/hydrodynamic settings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies abelian Chern-Simons theory on a strip with two boundaries, deriving general local Symanzik-consistent boundary conditions; it shows bulk equations fix boundary degrees of freedom via a broken gauge Ward identity, yielding counter-propagating chiral bosonic edge modes with opposite central charges, Tomonaga-Luttinger boundary actions, and a holographic bulk-boundary matching condition fixing edge velocities—robustly independent of strip width and symmetric setup assumptions.
AI.motivation: To establish a fully field-theoretic bulk-boundary correspondence for abelian Chern-Simons theory with two spatial boundaries, resolving the origin of counter-propagating chiral edge modes and their velocities without relying on model-dependent confining potentials—directly relevant to quantum Hall edge physics and topological hydrodynamics.
AI.method: Derivation of the most general local boundary conditions consistent with Symanzik power counting; analysis of gauge non-invariance at boundaries; use of broken gauge Ward identity to relate bulk equations of motion to boundary dynamics; construction of 2D boundary actions; imposition of consistency (holographic matching) between bulk Chern-Simons coupling and boundary parameters.
AI.result: Boundary degrees of freedom are uniquely fixed by bulk dynamics, giving rise to two Kac-Moody algebras with opposite central charges; boundary actions are Tomonaga-Luttinger type describing chiral bosons moving oppositely on each edge; a holographic matching condition determines edge velocities solely from Chern-Simons coupling and boundary parameters—ensuring velocity equality in magnitude and opposition in sign in symmetric setups, and independence from strip width.
AI.conclusion: The bulk-boundary correspondence in abelian Chern-Simons theory with two boundaries is rigorously realized within local quantum field theory: edge chirality, algebraic structure, and velocity quantization emerge intrinsically from boundary conditions and gauge symmetry breaking—not from external potentials—providing a universal field-theoretic foundation for quantum Hall edge transport and related topological systems.

title: Scalar axion field of toroidal electromagnetic pulses
summary: Axion electrodynamics extends Maxwell's theory by postulating a hypothetical pseudoscalar axion field sourced by a scalar product of electric and magnetic fields. In this work, we demonstrate that a superposition of toroidal electromagnetic pulses propagating in free space naturally exhibits localized regions, where $\bm{E}\cdot\bm{B}\ne0$. As a consequence of axion electrodynamics, these structured light pulses generate a space-time localized pseudoscalar field co-propagating with the pulses. This result should not be interpreted as a mechanism for generating axion particles by light, but rather as a consequence of adopting the axion electrodynamics extension to Maxwell's equations.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that toroidal electromagnetic pulses in free space naturally produce localized E·B ≠ 0 regions, thereby inducing a co-propagating pseudoscalar field within axion electrodynamics—without generating real axions.
AI.motivation: To explore observable consequences of axion electrodynamics (a theoretical extension of Maxwell's equations) in classical electromagnetic settings, specifically identifying field configurations where the axion source term E·B is non-zero in vacuum.
AI.method: Analytical and conceptual analysis of superposed toroidal electromagnetic pulses in free space; evaluation of the scalar invariant E·B and its spatiotemporal localization; interpretation within the framework of axion-modified Maxwell equations.
AI.result: Toroidal pulse superpositions yield localized, transient regions with E·B ≠ 0 in vacuum—serving as effective sources for a space-time-localized pseudoscalar (axion-like) field that co-propagates with the pulses.
AI.conclusion: The emergence of a dynamical pseudoscalar field from structured light is an inherent prediction of axion electrodynamics, distinct from axion particle production; it highlights how topological field structures can manifest axionic coupling classically.

title: ${\cal N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills thermodynamics to order $λ^{5/2}$
summary: We calculate the resummed perturbative free energy of ${\cal N} = 4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills in four spacetime dimensions (SYM$_{44}$) to order $λ^{5/2}$ in the 't Hooft coupling at finite temperature and zero chemical potential. All infrared divergences cancel when we include contributions from SYM$_{44}$ ring diagrams and the final result is both ultraviolet and infrared finite. Our result has special significance since order $λ^{5/2}$ is the highest order calculation that can be done with perturbation theory, because there are nonperturbative effects associated with the magnetic mass scale that come into play at order $λ^3$. We compare results obtained with regularization by dimensional reduction (RDR), which preserves supersymmetry, and canonical dimensional regularization (DR). We also compare with a generalized Padé approximant constructed by matching the weak coupling result at order $λ^2$ and the large $N_c$ strong coupling result at order $λ^{-3/2}$. Finally we make a comparison between our result and the QCD free energy and show that SYM$_{44}$ has better convergence properties.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the resummed perturbative free energy of N=4 SYM in 4D up to λ^{5/2} at finite temperature, achieving full UV and IR finiteness via ring diagram resummation; it compares regularization schemes (RDR vs DR), benchmarks against Padé approximants matching weak- and strong-coupling limits, and demonstrates superior convergence versus QCD.
AI.motivation: To extend finite-temperature perturbation theory for N=4 SYM beyond known orders while resolving infrared divergences; to probe the boundary of perturbative validity (λ^{5/2} is maximal before nonperturbative magnetic mass effects at λ^3 dominate); and to assess convergence and regularization dependence in a controlled supersymmetric setting.
AI.method: Resummed perturbation theory including hard thermal loop (HTL)–improved propagators and SYM_{44} ring (daisy) diagrams; dimensional reduction (RDR) and canonical dimensional regularization (DR) for UV regularization; comparison with generalized Padé approximant interpolating between weak-coupling (λ^2) and large-N_c strong-coupling (λ^{-3/2}) expansions.
AI.result: Finite, scheme-independent free energy up to O(λ^{5/2}); cancellation of all IR divergences upon inclusion of ring diagrams; quantitative agreement between RDR and DR within expected scheme dependence; Padé approximant shows good interpolation; SYM_{44} exhibits faster convergence than QCD free energy at comparable coupling.
AI.conclusion: The λ^{5/2} resummed free energy establishes the ultimate reach of thermal perturbation theory in N=4 SYM; confirms consistency of supersymmetric regularization (RDR); provides a high-precision benchmark for nonperturbative methods and strong-coupling extrapolations; and highlights the improved analyticity and convergence of maximally supersymmetric theories relative to QCD.

title: Doubly charged Higgs production within the Higgs triplet model at future electron-positron colliders
summary: We investigate in detail the discovery potential of the doubly charged Higgs boson at the Compact Linear Collider in $e^-e^-$, $e^-γ$, $γγ$, and $e^+e^-$ collision modes, within the Higgs triplet model at two extreme benchmark points as representatives of the Yukawa-like and gauge-like regions. In the Yukawa-like region, the most promising production mechanism is the single production via $e^-e^-$ and $e^-γ$ collisions. Given the subsequent decay of the doubly charged Higgs into a same-sign lepton pair, CLIC can achieve statistical significance well beyond the discovery threshold, within the parameter space permitted by experimental constraints. In the gauge-like region, with the $\ell^{\pm}\ell^{\pm} + \geq 3j$ final state, CLIC exhibits robust discovery potential for the doubly charged Higgs boson, up to a mass of approximately $1.2~\mathrm{TeV}$. We also investigate the search for doubly charged Higgs at the HL-LHC. Our results demonstrate that CLIC possesses greater advantages and offers superior discovery potential for the doubly charged Higgs boson, compared to the HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the discovery potential of the doubly charged Higgs boson (H^{±±}) at CLIC across multiple collision modes (e⁻e⁻, e⁻γ, γγ, e⁺e⁻) within the Higgs triplet model, comparing two benchmark regions—Yukawa-like and gauge-like—and contrasting CLIC’s sensitivity with that of HL-LHC.
AI.motivation: To assess whether future lepton colliders—particularly CLIC—can decisively probe the doubly charged Higgs boson in parameter regions inaccessible or poorly constrained at hadron colliders like HL-LHC, especially given complementary production mechanisms and cleaner final states.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological study: cross section calculations for H^{±±} production in e⁻e⁻, e⁻γ, γγ, and e⁺e⁻ channels; event simulation and statistical significance estimation (using Poisson statistics and background estimation) for key decay channels (ℓ±ℓ± and ℓ±ℓ± + ≥3j); comparison against current experimental bounds (e.g., LEP, LHC, low-energy precision tests); benchmarking in Yukawa-like vs. gauge-like coupling regimes of the Higgs triplet model.
AI.result: In the Yukawa-like region, e⁻e⁻ and e⁻γ single production dominates, enabling high-significance discovery of H^{±±} → ℓ±ℓ± up to ~1 TeV; in the gauge-like region, the ℓ±ℓ± + ≥3j channel yields robust discovery reach up to ~1.2 TeV. CLIC outperforms HL-LHC across both regions due to higher luminosity, cleaner environment, and enhanced sensitivity to leptonic decays and suppressed QCD backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: CLIC offers superior and complementary discovery potential for the doubly charged Higgs boson compared to HL-LHC, particularly in the Higgs triplet model’s theoretically motivated coupling regimes—making it a pivotal facility for probing left-right symmetry and neutrino mass generation mechanisms.

title: The 't Hooft loop from a center-vortex wave functional
summary: Previously, we proposed an infrared vacuum wave functional for $SU(N)$ Yang-Mills theory peaked at thin center vortices and showed that it yields an area law for the Wilson loop. In this work, we use this wave functional to calculate the spatial 't Hooft loop, for which we find a perimeter law, in accordance with 't Hooft's criterion for confinement.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the spatial 't Hooft loop using an infrared vacuum wave functional peaked at thin center vortices in SU(N) Yang-Mills theory and finds a perimeter law, confirming 't Hooft's confinement criterion.
AI.motivation: To verify 't Hooft's confinement criterion by evaluating the behavior of the spatial 't Hooft loop within a vortex-based vacuum wave functional framework.
AI.method: Uses a previously constructed infrared vacuum wave functional for SU(N) Yang-Mills theory, peaked at thin center vortices, to compute the expectation value of the spatial 't Hooft loop.
AI.result: The spatial 't Hooft loop exhibits a perimeter law, consistent with dual superconductivity and 't Hooft's confinement criterion.
AI.conclusion: The vortex-peaked wave functional correctly reproduces both area-law Wilson loops and perimeter-law 't Hooft loops, supporting center-vortex dominance in confinement.

title: Monte-Carlo Event Generation for X-Ray Thomson Scattering Analysis
summary: A key diagnostic in warm-dense matter (WDM) experiments is X-ray Thomson scattering (XRTS), but its interpretation is often limited by complex instrument effects and the high computationally expensive combinations of microscopic models with detector simulations. We present a proof-of-principle implementation of an event-driven approach to XRTS modelling, inspired by particle physics event-generators. Instead of computing the spectra via forward models, individual scattering events are sampled from the differential cross section and sent through a spectrometer simulation. This provides a statistically consistent representation that preserves full kinematic information and enables flexible and geometry-aware analysis. We demonstrate the feasibility and physical consistency of the method for non-resonant XRTS in a synthetic setup. By decoupling event generation from detector-level analysis, the framework allows efficient reuse of the sampled events and reduces computational overhead associated with repeated evaluations. The method is model-agnostic and establishes a new connection between particle-physics event generation techniques and WDM diagnostics, providing a scalable foundation for advanced XRTS analysis and inference.

AI.tldr: Introduces an event-driven XRTS modelling framework—inspired by particle physics event generators—that samples individual scattering events from the differential cross section and propagates them through spectrometer simulations, enabling statistically consistent, geometry-aware, and computationally efficient analysis of warm-dense matter.
AI.motivation: Interpretation of X-ray Thomson scattering (XRTS) in warm-dense matter experiments is hindered by complex instrument effects and high computational cost of coupling microscopic models with detector simulations.
AI.method: Event-driven Monte Carlo approach: scattering events are sampled directly from the differential cross section and propagated through a detailed spectrometer simulation; decouples event generation from detector-level analysis; model-agnostic and preserves full kinematic information.
AI.result: Demonstrated feasibility and physical consistency for non-resonant XRTS in a synthetic setup; enables flexible, geometry-aware analysis; reduces computational overhead via event reuse; supports scalable inference and advanced diagnostics.
AI.conclusion: The method establishes a novel bridge between particle-physics event-generation techniques and WDM diagnostics, providing a scalable, statistically rigorous, and computationally efficient foundation for next-generation XRTS analysis.

title: Holographic entanglement entropy, Wilson loops, and neural networks
summary: We apply artificial neural networks to the holographic inverse problem, reconstructing bulk geometry from boundary entanglement entropy by using the Ryu--Takayanagi area functional as a differentiable loss. Validated on the AdS-Schwarzschild background, this approach recovers the blackening factor to 1.7% accuracy. For finite-density backgrounds like the Gubser--Rocha model, we demonstrate that strip entanglement entropy determines only the spatial metric. We resolve this exact one-function degeneracy by incorporating holographic Wilson loop data, which couples to the timelike metric. We present a semi-analytical inversion combining Bilson's and Hashimoto's formulas, alongside a general three-network variational method minimizing the combined area and Nambu--Goto actions. The neural network achieves sub-0.2% accuracy for both metric functions without closed-form derivative relations, establishing a flexible framework for integrating multiple holographic observables.

AI.tldr: This paper uses artificial neural networks to solve the holographic inverse problem—reconstructing bulk spacetime geometry from boundary entanglement entropy and Wilson loop data—achieving high accuracy (≤0.2%) on AdS-Schwarzschild and Gubser–Rocha backgrounds via differentiable geometric loss functions.
AI.motivation: To overcome the ill-posedness and functional degeneracy in reconstructing bulk geometry from boundary data in holography, especially when entanglement entropy alone is insufficient (e.g., cannot determine timelike metric components in finite-density backgrounds).
AI.method: Employs differentiable neural networks trained on Ryu–Takayanagi area functional (for entanglement entropy) and Nambu–Goto action (for Wilson loops) as loss terms; combines semi-analytical inversion (Bilson’s + Hashimoto’s formulas) with a three-network variational architecture to jointly infer spatial and temporal metric components.
AI.result: Reconstructs AdS-Schwarzschild blackening factor with 1.7% error; resolves one-function degeneracy in Gubser–Rocha model by adding Wilson loop data; achieves sub-0.2% accuracy for both metric functions without requiring closed-form derivatives.
AI.conclusion: Neural networks provide a robust, flexible, and derivative-free framework for multi-observable holographic reconstruction, enabling precise inference of bulk geometry beyond entanglement entropy alone.

title: Quarkyonic Meson Matter for Finite Isospin Density
comment: To be published in a special volume of Acta Physica Polonica B dedicated to Andrzej Bialas on the occasion of his 90'th birthday
summary: QCD at finite isospin density is considered for a large number of colors $N_c$. A linear sigma model is used to model the meson content of the theory at low density. At isospin chemical potential $μ_I << Λ_{QCD}$, this matter forms a Bose condensate. For $μ_I >> \sqrt{N_c} Λ_{QCD}$, unlike QCD remains confined, but the degrees of freedom of the system are mesons and Cooper pairs bound on size scales small compared to the QCD size scale determined by the superfluid gap. For most purposes this matter may be analyzed using weak coupling methods. For $ Λ_{QCD} \le μ_I \le \sqrt{Nc} Λ_{QCD}$, we argue that meson matter is quarkyonic, with quarks bound into mesons on a size scale of order $Λ_{QCD}$ corresponding to a filled Fermi sea of quarks, with possible Bose condensation at the Fermi surface and/or Cooper pairs with finite width of the surface of order $Λ_{QCD}$.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes QCD at finite isospin density in the large-Nc limit, identifying three distinct regimes based on the isospin chemical potential μ_I: a low-density Bose-condensed mesonic phase, a high-density weakly-coupled meson-Cooper-pair phase, and an intermediate 'quarkyonic' regime where quarks form a Fermi sea bound into mesons with possible surface condensation or finite-width Cooper pairing.
AI.motivation: To understand the phase structure of QCD at finite isospin chemical potential in the large-Nc limit, bridging between perturbative and non-perturbative regimes and clarifying the nature of matter where both confinement and Fermi surface effects coexist.
AI.method: Analytical analysis using large-Nc scaling arguments combined with a linear sigma model for low-energy mesonic degrees of freedom; identification and characterization of distinct asymptotic regimes based on scaling of μ_I relative to Λ_QCD and √N_c Λ_QCD.
AI.result: Three qualitatively distinct phases are identified: (i) μ_I ≪ Λ_QCD → mesonic Bose condensate; (ii) μ_I ≫ √N_c Λ_QCD → weakly-coupled regime dominated by mesons and small-size Cooper pairs; (iii) Λ_QCD ≤ μ_I ≤ √N_c Λ_QCD → 'quarkyonic' meson matter with quark Fermi sea, confinement at scale Λ_QCD, and possible surface Bose condensation or finite-width Cooper pairing.
AI.conclusion: QCD at finite isospin density exhibits a rich phase structure in the large-Nc limit, with an intermediate quarkyonic regime that combines features of both confined and degenerate matter—distinct from standard nuclear or quark matter—where mesons remain the effective low-energy degrees of freedom despite underlying quark Fermi statistics.

title: Background Fields Meet the Heat Kernel: Gauge Invariance and RGEs without diagrams
summary: We introduce a new method that exploits the combination of the Heat Kernel (HK) and Background Field Method to compute gauge-invariant and gauge parameter-independent quantities such as the effective potential, anomalous dimensions, and renormalization group equations. In contrast to currently employed techniques, these results are obtained exclusively from the dynamics of the background fields, without relying on supplementary input from, e.g., traditional diagrammatic calculations. This is achieved by a consistent treatment of open and closed derivatives in the HK expansions. In this way, we compute the standard quantities such as $β$ functions and their gauge-parameter independence when background fields are on-shell. We demonstrate this formalism for instructive examples such as Scalar QED and Yukawa theory. Full results for the bosonic part of the Standard Model provide further validation of our approach.

AI.tldr: A new method combining Heat Kernel and Background Field Method computes gauge-invariant, gauge-parameter-independent quantum effective quantities (e.g., β functions, anomalous dimensions) solely from background field dynamics—without diagrammatic input—via consistent handling of open/closed derivatives in HK expansions; validated in Scalar QED, Yukawa theory, and the bosonic Standard Model.
AI.motivation: To compute gauge-invariant and gauge-parameter-independent physical quantities (e.g., effective potential, β functions, anomalous dimensions) without relying on traditional diagrammatic techniques or gauge-dependent intermediate steps.
AI.method: Combines the Heat Kernel (HK) expansion with the Background Field Method, introducing a consistent treatment of open and closed derivatives in the HK series to ensure gauge invariance and gauge-parameter independence; computations are performed entirely within the background-field formalism, with on-shell background fields.
AI.result: Derives gauge-parameter-independent β functions, anomalous dimensions, and renormalization group equations for Scalar QED, Yukawa theory, and the bosonic sector of the Standard Model—all obtained exclusively from background-field dynamics without diagrammatic input.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a self-contained, manifestly gauge-invariant framework for computing renormalization-group quantities, eliminating dependence on gauge-fixing parameters and auxiliary diagrammatic calculations, thereby enhancing conceptual clarity and computational efficiency in quantum field theory.

authors: Maria Teresa Núñez Pardo de Vera
title: The SUSY reach of Higgs Factories in the most challenging scenario: scalar $τ$-leptons with lowest cross section and small mass differences
summary: The direct pair-production of the $\tildeτ$, is one of the most interesting channels to search for SUSY in: the $\tildeτ$ is likely to be the lightest of the scalar leptons, and the signature of $\tildeτ$ pair production is one of the experimentally most difficult ones, making it the ``worst'' possible scenario for SUSY searches. The current limit on $\tildeτ$ production in the general MSSM comes from LEP. Limits obtained at LHC do extend to higher masses, but they are only valid under strong assumptions. Future $e^+e^-$ colliders will be powerful for SUSY searches, offering advantages with respect to previous $e^+e^-$ colliders as well as to hadron machines. In order to quantify their capabilities, the ``worst-case'' scenario for $\tildeτ$ searches has been studied, taking into account the effect of the $\tildeτ$ mixing on both $\tildeτ$ production cross section and on detection efficiency. To evaluate the latter, the ILD detector concept, originally developed for the International Linear Collider (ILC), and the ILC beam conditions at a centre-of-mass energy of $500$\,GeV have been used for detailed simulations, including for the first time the effect of bunch-crossings containing no hard $e^+e^-$ interaction, but only low-$\it{P_{T}}$ hadrons from $γγ$ interactions and $e^+e^-$ pairs from beamstrahlung. Still, the obtained exclusion and discovery reaches extend nearly up to the kinematic limit even in the worst-case scenario. This remains true also when the $\tildeτ$ and the lightest SUSY particle are quite close in mass. The results of the detailed study are extrapolated to centre-of-mass energies, integrated luminosities and beam polarisations of other proposed Higgs factory projects and discussed in view of their respective experimental environments, in particular addressing the case of FCCee.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the capability of future e+e- colliders, especially the ILC and FCCee, to detect stau (τ̃) pair production—the most challenging SUSY search channel—under worst-case assumptions including stau mixing and realistic beam backgrounds; detailed ILD detector simulations at 500 GeV show near-kinematic-limit sensitivity even for compressed spectra.
AI.motivation: The direct pair-production of the lightest scalar lepton, the stau (τ̃), is a critical yet experimentally challenging SUSY search channel due to its low cross section, difficult signatures (e.g., soft taus), and potential mass degeneracy with the lightest SUSY particle (LSP); current LHC limits rely on strong model assumptions, while LEP limits are outdated—hence the need to quantify the discovery potential of future e+e− colliders in the most pessimistic ('worst-case') scenario.
AI.method: A detailed Monte Carlo study using the ILD detector concept and ILC beam conditions (500 GeV c.m. energy) was performed, incorporating stau mixing effects on both production cross section and detection efficiency; for the first time, beam-induced backgrounds—specifically γγ→hadrons and beamstrahlung e+e− pairs from empty bunch crossings—were included in full simulation; results were extrapolated to other Higgs factory proposals (e.g., FCCee) considering their distinct c.m. energies, integrated luminosities, and beam polarizations.
AI.result: Even in the worst-case scenario—including maximal stau mixing, compressed τ̃–LSP mass spectrum, and realistic beam-induced backgrounds—the ILC at 500 GeV achieves stau exclusion and discovery reaches approaching the kinematic limit (∼250 GeV); this robustness holds across varied experimental configurations, and extrapolations confirm strong sensitivity for FCCee and similar e+e− facilities.
AI.conclusion: Future high-luminosity e+e− colliders—particularly those with polarized beams and advanced vertex/tau identification like ILD—are uniquely capable of probing the theoretically favored but experimentally elusive stau sector up to the kinematic limit, even under maximally challenging conditions; this establishes them as indispensable tools for comprehensive SUSY searches beyond LHC reach.

title: Are Black Holes Fuzzballs? Probing Horizon-Scale Structure with LISA
summary: Gravitational waves provide a unique probe of the strong-field regime of gravity, offering access to physics beyond the classical black hole paradigm. We explore how space-based observations of extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) can be used to test the fuzzball proposal, a quantum gravity-inspired alternative to Kerr black holes. By introducing generic multipolar deformations encoding potential symmetry breakings and performing a systematic parameter estimation analysis, we forecast LISA's ability to constrain deviations from the Kerr geometry in the near-horizon region. We show that EMRI signals with realistic signal-to-noise ratios can constrain multiple higher-order multipoles at levels orders of magnitude beyond current electromagnetic and ground-based gravitational-wave bounds, opening a new observational window onto horizon-scale structure. In particular, we find that LISA can constrain generic non-axisymmetric mass quadrupole deformations at the $10^{-3}$ level and axisymmetric mass octupole deformations at the $10^{-2}$ level, providing concrete observational targets for identifying fuzzball geometries. Our results demonstrate that precision measurements of EMRI waveforms will transform LISA into a powerful laboratory for fundamental physics and offer the first direct empirical constraints on quantum-gravity-motivated models of compact objects.

AI.tldr: This paper forecasts LISA's capability to test the fuzzball proposal—quantum-gravity alternatives to Kerr black holes—using extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), by constraining generic multipolar deviations from Kerr geometry in the near-horizon region.
AI.motivation: To empirically test quantum-gravity-motivated alternatives to classical black holes (specifically the fuzzball proposal) using gravitational-wave observations of EMRIs, where horizon-scale structure may imprint detectable multipolar deformations.
AI.method: Introduces generic, symmetry-breaking multipolar deformations to Kerr geometry; performs systematic Bayesian parameter estimation on simulated LISA EMRI waveforms to forecast constraints on mass quadrupole (non-axisymmetric) and octupole (axisymmetric) deformations.
AI.result: LISA can constrain non-axisymmetric mass quadrupole deformations at ~10⁻³ and axisymmetric mass octupole deformations at ~10⁻² levels—orders of magnitude tighter than current electromagnetic or ground-based GW bounds.
AI.conclusion: Precision EMRI waveform measurements with LISA will provide the first direct empirical constraints on quantum-gravity models of compact objects, turning LISA into a fundamental physics laboratory for probing horizon-scale structure.

title: $ξRφ^2$ non-minimal coupling, and the long range gravitational potential for different spin fields from 2-2 scattering amplitudes
summary: In this paper we investigate the long range gravitational effect of curvature-scalar field non-minimal coupling, in the form of $ξR φ^2$, in the perturbative quantum gravity framework. Such coupling is most naturally motivated from the renormalisation of a scalar field theory with a quartic self interaction in a curved spacetime background. This coupling results in two scalar-$n$ graviton vertices which contain no explicit momenta of the scalar, qualitatively different from the usual, e.g. $κh^{μν}T_{μν}$-type minimal matter-graviton vertices. Assuming the dimensionless coupling parameter $ξ$ to be small, we compute the 2-2 scattering Feynman amplitudes between such scalars up to ${\cal O}(G^2 ξ)$. From the non-relativistic limit of these amplitudes, we compute the corresponding long range gravitational potential. There exists no tree level contribution $({\cal O}(ξG))$ here, and hence the one loop ${\cal O}(G^2 ξ)$ result is leading. Recently, the effect of a cosmological constant in such non-minimal interaction and the subsequent gravitational potential was computed. In this work we take the cosmological constant to be vanishing. The resulting potential is found to have $r^{-4}$ leading behaviour. We further extend these results for scalar-massive spin-1 and massive spin-1/2 scattering. Spin and polarisation dependence of the two body potential have been explicitly demonstrated. We discuss some possible physical implications of these results.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the long-range gravitational potential arising from a non-minimal curvature-scalar coupling $ξRφ^2$ in perturbative quantum gravity, finding a leading $r^{-4}$ behavior at one-loop ${\cal O}(G^2 ξ)$, with extensions to scalar interactions with massive spin-1 and spin-1/2 fields, including explicit spin/polarization dependence.
AI.motivation: The non-minimal coupling $ξRφ^2$ arises naturally from renormalizing a scalar field with quartic self-interaction in curved spacetime; its gravitational effects—distinct from minimal coupling due to momentum-independent vertices—are poorly understood in the long-range regime.
AI.method: Perturbative quantum gravity: compute 2→2 scattering amplitudes for scalars coupled via $ξRφ^2$ up to ${\cal O}(G^2 ξ)$; extract non-relativistic limit to obtain static potential; extend to scalar–massive spin-1 and spin-1/2 scattering using appropriate propagators and vertices; assume small dimensionless $ξ$, vanishing cosmological constant.
AI.result: The leading long-range potential is $\propto r^{-4}$, emerging solely at one-loop order ${\cal O}(G^2 ξ)$ (no tree-level ${\cal O}(ξG)$ contribution); spin- and polarization-dependent potentials are derived for scalar–vector and scalar–fermion systems.
AI.conclusion: Non-minimal curvature-coupling generates a distinctive, spin-sensitive $r^{-4}$ gravitational potential beyond Newtonian and post-Newtonian expectations, implying novel phenomenology for scalar-mediated long-range forces in quantum gravity contexts.

title: Comments on Symmetry Operators, Asymptotic Charges and Soft Theorems
summary: We study the relation between emergent 1-form symmetries and soft photon theorems in QED. We show that in the relevant massive and massless kinematic regimes, described respectively by HQET and SCET, the soft sector admits electric and magnetic 1-form symmetries. We then show that these symmetries give rise to an infinite-dimensional Abelian algebra of ordinary conserved charges, with a central extension. In Minkowski spacetime, suitable choices of hypersurfaces reduce these charges to the familiar asymptotic symmetry charges and imply the leading electric and magnetic soft photon theorems. We further show that the central term in this algebra fixes a contact term appearing in scattering amplitudes involving two soft photons with mixed electric-magnetic polarizations. Finally, we extend the same construction to inclusive observables and apply it to QED photon detectors.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a connection between emergent 1-form symmetries in soft sectors of QED (in HQET and SCET) and soft photon theorems, deriving asymptotic symmetry charges, recovering leading electric/magnetic soft theorems, fixing a mixed-polarization two-soft-photon contact term via the central extension, and extending the framework to inclusive observables and photon detectors.
AI.motivation: To uncover the underlying symmetry origin of soft photon theorems in QED by identifying emergent higher-form symmetries in the infrared soft sector.
AI.method: Analyzes the soft sectors of QED using effective field theories (HQET for massive and SCET for massless kinematics), constructs electric and magnetic 1-form symmetries, derives their associated infinite-dimensional Abelian charge algebra with central extension, relates charges to asymptotic symmetries on appropriate hypersurfaces in Minkowski space, and extends analysis to inclusive observables and detector models.
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of electric/magnetic 1-form symmetries in soft QED; derives infinite-dimensional Abelian charge algebra with central extension; recovers leading soft photon theorems as Ward identities; fixes a specific contact term in two-soft-photon amplitudes via the central charge; generalizes construction to inclusive observables and QED photon detectors.
AI.conclusion: Soft photon theorems in QED are manifestations of emergent electric and magnetic 1-form symmetries in the infrared, encoded in a centrally extended charge algebra whose structure governs both asymptotic symmetries and subleading amplitude data.

title: Massive Exchange and the Sign of the Equilateral Bispectrum
summary: We study the inflationary bispectrum generated by the tree-level exchange of a massive hidden-sector scalar during inflation. When the interaction between the inflaton and the hidden sector arises only from the leading boost-breaking operator of the Effective Field Theory (EFT) of inflation, the equilateral bispectrum for principal-series scalar exchange is known to be universally negative, independent of the sign of the coupling. We revisit this result within the full EFT operator basis. Using bootstrap methods, we construct the de Sitter-invariant seed four-point function and obtain the inflationary bispectrum via weight-shifting operators and a soft-limit procedure. While the equilateral bispectrum remains strictly negative when only the leading interaction is present, additional operators generate independent cubic structures whose contributions compete in the equilateral configuration. As a result, the sign of the bispectrum is no longer universal. We derive a critical ratio of interaction coefficients that separates regions of positive and negative equilateral bispectrum. We further study the effects of reduced sound speed $c_s<1$ and the exchange of multiple particles. In both cases, the critical ratio is modified, and for multi-particle exchange a positive equilateral bispectrum can arise even when the higher-order operator is subdominant. Our results show that the negativity of the equilateral bispectrum from massive exchange is not generic, but reflects a restricted operator structure in the EFT of inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the sign of the inflationary equilateral bispectrum from massive hidden-sector scalar exchange in the EFT of inflation, showing that universality (strict negativity) breaks when higher-order boost-breaking operators are included; it derives a critical coupling ratio determining the sign, and extends analysis to $c_s < 1$ and multi-particle exchange, finding that positivity can emerge even with subdominant higher-order interactions.
AI.motivation: To test the claimed universality of a negative equilateral bispectrum from principal-series scalar exchange in EFT of inflation — a result derived under the assumption of only the leading boost-breaking operator — and determine whether it persists in the full EFT operator basis.
AI.method: Uses bootstrap methods to construct the de Sitter-invariant seed four-point function, applies weight-shifting operators and a soft-limit procedure to obtain the inflationary bispectrum, and systematically includes all relevant cubic EFT operators beyond the leading one; analyzes modifications due to reduced sound speed and multi-particle exchange.
AI.result: The equilateral bispectrum is no longer universally negative once higher-order EFT operators are included; a critical ratio of interaction coefficients determines its sign; reduced sound speed and multi-particle exchange modify this critical ratio, and in the latter case, a positive equilateral bispectrum can arise even if the higher-order operator is subdominant.
AI.conclusion: The negativity of the equilateral bispectrum from massive scalar exchange is not generic but an artifact of truncating the EFT at the leading operator; full EFT consistency allows for both signs, with observational implications for primordial non-Gaussianity constraints.

title: Geodesics from Quantum Field Theory: A Case Study in AdS
summary: Localized one-particle states of a quantum field theory--whether in flat space or on a curved background--are expected to exhibit geodesic motion in an appropriate semiclassical regime. This expectation is often invoked heuristically: in this work we develop two precise implementations and test them in detail in global AdS$_3$. First, we define a covariant ''center-of-mass'' trajectory from the expectation value of the stress tensor operator and show, using only $\nabla_μ\langle T^{μν}\rangle=0$, that it obeys the geodesic equation in the monopole (sufficiently localized) approximation in a general spacetime. This provides a QFT-in-curved-spacetime generalization of the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon framework in classical general relativity. Second, we construct position operators from the Klein--Gordon inner product and mode completeness, and compute their expectation values in generic single-particle wave packet states. We then build explicit normalizable wave packets of a free scalar field in empty AdS$_3$ with tunable energy and angular momentum, and demonstrate analytically and numerically that both prescriptions reproduce the expected radial, circular, and elliptical-like timelike and null geodesics. Our discussion also isolates a natural ultra-relativistic regime in which the wave packet trajectory exhibits a controlled crossover from timelike to null geodesic behavior. We identify precise limits where the localized geodesic interpretation of the wave packet breaks down. On the CFT side, we show that bulk localization--specifically the radial data--is captured by how the state is distributed over global descendants of the dual primary.

AI.tldr: This paper develops two rigorous QFT-based methods to define localized particle trajectories in curved spacetimes—specifically global AdS₃—and shows both yield geodesic motion in the semiclassical, monopole limit; it analytically and numerically verifies agreement with timelike/null geodesics for explicit normalizable wave packets, identifies breakdown limits, and connects bulk localization to CFT descendant structure.
AI.motivation: To provide precise, covariant, and physically grounded definitions of 'localized one-particle states' in QFT on curved backgrounds—moving beyond heuristic appeals to geodesic motion—and to rigorously test their semiclassical trajectory behavior in a controlled setting (global AdS₃).
AI.method: 1) Defines a stress-tensor-based center-of-mass trajectory via ⟨T^μν⟩ and uses ∇_μ⟨T^μν⟩ = 0 to derive geodesic motion in the monopole approximation; 2) Constructs position operators from Klein–Gordon inner product and mode completeness, computes their expectation values in single-particle wave packets; constructs explicit normalizable scalar wave packets in AdS₃ with tunable E and L; performs analytical and numerical trajectory analysis; maps bulk radial localization to CFT global descendant distribution.
AI.result: Both prescriptions reproduce exact timelike, circular, and elliptical-like geodesics in AdS₃; reveal a controlled ultra-relativistic crossover from timelike to null geodesic behavior; identify precise limits (e.g., delocalization, high curvature, or low energy) where geodesic interpretation breaks down; establish that radial localization is encoded in the CFT state's distribution over global descendants of the dual primary.
AI.conclusion: Localized QFT particle states in curved spacetime admit well-defined, covariant semiclassical trajectories governed by geodesic motion—generalizing classical frameworks like Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon—and this behavior is robust, testable, and holographically interpretable in AdS/CFT.
